business_glossary_term: Distribution Direct Store Delivery (DSD) Route ID
description: Unique identifier for the DSD route record. Primary key.
Foreign key linking to logistics.carrier. Business justification: DSD route planning assigns a carrier to each route; the carrier_id FK enables carrier performance and cost analysis.
Identifier of the distribution center or depot from which this DSD route originates. Links to the facility master.
Foreign key linking to logistics.lane. Business justification: DSD route aligns with a transport lane to calculate distance, fuel surcharge, and service level expectations.
Identifier of the driver or sales representative permanently or primarily assigned to this route. May be null for unassigned or pool routes.
Identifier of the sales or service territory to which this route is assigned. Used for sales force alignment and performance tracking.
Historical average order value per stop on this route in local currency. Used for revenue forecasting and route profitability analysis.
Timestamp when this route record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
Three-letter ISO currency code for monetary values associated with this route (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
Date when this route configuration was discontinued or superseded. Null for currently active routes. Used for historical route analysis.
Date when this route configuration became active and operational. Used for historical route analysis and change tracking.
Estimated total driving time for the route in minutes, excluding stop service time. Used for driver shift planning and OTIF performance targets.
Estimated total time spent at customer stops for unloading, merchandising, and order processing in minutes. Combined with drive time for total route duration.
Timestamp when this route record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit trail.
Date when this route was last reviewed and optimized for efficiency. Used to identify routes due for re-evaluation.
Boolean flag indicating whether this route includes merchandising activities (shelf stocking, display setup, POG compliance) in addition to delivery. True if merchandising is part of the service.
Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or route-specific considerations (e.g., 'Avoid highway during rush hour', 'Customer prefers morning delivery').
Total count of retail store or customer locations included in this route. Used for route capacity planning and driver workload estimation.
Target OSA percentage for stores on this route, representing the expected in-stock rate at point of sale. Used for DSD execution quality and replenishment effectiveness tracking.

business_glossary_term: On Time In Full (OTIF) Target Percentage
description: Target OTIF performance percentage for this route, representing the expected rate of deliveries completed on time and in full. Used for SLA management and driver performance evaluation.
Standard departure time from the DC for this route in HH:MM format (24-hour clock). Used for driver scheduling and DC loading dock coordination.
Expected return time to the DC for this route in HH:MM format (24-hour clock). Used for driver shift planning and vehicle turnaround scheduling.
Numeric priority ranking of this route relative to other routes in the territory or DC, with lower numbers indicating higher priority. Used for resource allocation during capacity constraints.
Boolean flag indicating whether this route requires temperature-controlled (refrigerated or frozen) transportation for product integrity. True if cold chain is required.
Boolean flag indicating whether the driver assigned to this route must hold hazmat certification due to regulated products (e.g., aerosols, flammables). True if certification is required.
Business identifier for the DSD route, used for operational reference and scheduling. Typically alphanumeric code assigned by logistics planning.
Human-readable name or description of the DSD route, often including geographic or customer identifiers (e.g., 'Downtown Metro Route A', 'North Region Convenience Stores').

Calculated efficiency score for this route based on distance, time, stops, and revenue, typically ranging from 0-100. Higher scores indicate more optimized routes. Used for continuous improvement initiatives.

Current operational status of the DSD route. Active routes are in regular service; inactive routes are permanently discontinued; suspended routes are temporarily paused; under_review routes are being optimized; seasonal_closed routes are off-season.

Classification of the DSD route based on service model: standard (regular scheduled delivery), express (same-day or expedited), bulk (high-volume customers), emergency (unplanned replenishment), seasonal (temporary routes for peak demand).
Comma-separated list of days of the week this route is scheduled to run (e.g., 'Mon,Wed,Fri' for a three-day-per-week route). Supports recurring schedule planning.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the route start point (typically the DC or depot). Used for route optimization and GPS tracking.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the route start point (typically the DC or depot). Used for route optimization and GPS tracking.
Total driving distance for the complete route in kilometers, from DC departure through all stops and return. Used for fuel cost estimation and vehicle range planning.
Minimum vehicle cargo capacity required in standard units (cases, pallets, or cubic meters) to fulfill typical route demand. Used for vehicle assignment.
Type of vehicle required to service this route based on cargo volume, weight, and product requirements (e.g., refrigerated for cold chain products).
Primary key for facility

Foreign key linking to sustainability.esg_commitment. Business justification: Facilities have specific ESG commitments (energy, waste, emissions) that are tracked for performance dashboards and compliance.

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Tracks the facility manager employee for each distribution center, required for operational performance metrics and compliance reporting.
Primary street address line for the distribution center facility. Organizational contact data classified as confidential business information.
Secondary address line for suite, building, or unit information. Organizational contact data classified as confidential business information.
City or municipality where the distribution center is located. Organizational contact data classified as confidential business information.
Date when the distribution center ceased operations. Null for active facilities. Used for historical analysis and network optimization studies.
Primary contact email address for the distribution center. Organizational contact data classified as confidential business information.
Primary contact phone number for the distribution center. Organizational contact data classified as confidential business information.
Three-letter ISO country code where the distribution center is located.
Timestamp when this distribution center record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
Indicates whether the facility supports cross-docking operations where inbound goods are directly transferred to outbound shipments with minimal storage time.
Standard frequency in days for cycle counting inventory at this facility. Used for inventory accuracy management and audit compliance.
Business identifier code for the distribution center used across operational systems. Externally-known unique code for the facility.
Official business name of the distribution center or warehouse facility.
Number of dock doors designated for inbound receiving operations. Impacts receiving throughput capacity and scheduling.
Number of dock doors designated for outbound shipping operations. Impacts shipping throughput capacity and carrier scheduling.
Indicates whether this facility serves as a DSD hub for direct-to-retail delivery operations. DSD hubs bypass traditional distribution channels for faster store replenishment.

Classification of the distribution center based on temperature control and operational model. Ambient for room temperature, chilled for refrigerated, frozen for sub-zero, multi-temperature for mixed zones, DSD hub for Direct Store Delivery operations, cross-dock for flow-through distribution.
Indicates whether the facility is certified under FSC chain of custody standards for sustainable sourcing. Required for handling FSC-certified paper and wood-based products.
reference: Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) Chain of Custody Certification

description: Indicates whether the facility is certified under Good Manufacturing Practice standards. Required for handling cosmetics, personal care, and certain consumer goods products.
reference: ISO 22716 Good Manufacturing Practices for Cosmetics

description: Indicates whether the facility is certified to handle and store hazardous materials. Required for distribution of products with EPA or OSHA regulated substances.

Primary inventory rotation method used at this facility. FIFO (First In First Out) for standard goods, FEFO (First Expired First Out) for perishables and date-sensitive products, LIFO (Last In First Out) for specific use cases.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the distribution center in decimal degrees. Used for geospatial analytics, route optimization, and logistics planning.
Expiration date of the facility lease agreement. Null for owned facilities. Used for lease renewal planning and facility strategy.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the distribution center in decimal degrees. Used for geospatial analytics, route optimization, and logistics planning.
Timestamp when this distribution center record was last modified. Audit trail for change tracking and data quality monitoring.
Date when the distribution center commenced operations. Used for facility age analysis and depreciation calculations.
Standard operating hours for weekdays in format HH:MM-HH:MM. Used for scheduling inbound deliveries, outbound shipments, and workforce planning.
Standard operating hours for weekends in format HH:MM-HH:MM. Used for scheduling weekend operations and carrier coordination.

Current operational state of the distribution center in its lifecycle. Active indicates full operations, inactive for temporarily closed, under construction for new facilities being built, decommissioned for permanently closed, seasonal for facilities operating only during peak periods, maintenance for temporary closure due to upgrades or repairs.
Target OSA performance percentage for stores served by this distribution center. OSA measures product availability at retail shelf level.

business_glossary_term: On Time In Full (OTIF) Target Percentage
description: Target OTIF performance percentage for this distribution center. OTIF measures the percentage of orders delivered on time and in full, a key supply chain KPI.
Classification of facility ownership model. Owned for company-owned facilities, leased for long-term leased properties, third-party logistics for 3PL-operated warehouses.
Postal or ZIP code for the distribution center address. Organizational contact data classified as confidential business information.
SAP S/4HANA plant code representing this distribution center in the ERP system. Maps to the SAP MM and WM modules for material management and warehouse management.
SAP S/4HANA storage location code within the plant. Represents the primary storage location identifier for inventory transactions in SAP WM module.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Storage Location Master Data

description: Number of operational shifts per day at the facility. Used for labor planning, throughput capacity modeling, and operational cost analysis.
State, province, or regional administrative division where the facility is located. Organizational contact data classified as confidential business information.
Maximum number of pallet positions available for storage. Key metric for inventory capacity planning and space utilization analysis.
Indicates whether the facility has temperature-controlled storage zones. True for facilities with chilled or frozen capabilities, false for ambient-only.
IANA time zone identifier for the distribution center location. Used for scheduling, shift planning, and cross-facility coordination.
Total warehouse floor space capacity in square feet. Includes all storage, staging, and operational areas within the facility.
Unique site identifier in the Blue Yonder WMS system. Used for integration and synchronization between the lakehouse and the operational WMS platform.
Primary key for the offset_allocation association
Foreign key linking to carbon_offset
Foreign key linking to distribution_facility
Quantity of carbon offset (tCO2e) allocated to the facility
Date the offset amount was allocated to the facility
Primary key for storage_location
Identifier of the parent distribution center facility where this storage location resides.
Velocity-based classification of the location for slotting optimization: A (high-velocity/fast-moving), B (medium-velocity), C (low-velocity/slow-moving).
Aisle designation within the warehouse layout for physical navigation and picking route optimization.
Bay or column position within the aisle for precise horizontal location reference.
Specific bin or slot position within the level for granular inventory placement and retrieval.
Date when the storage location was blocked or made unavailable for operations.
Explanation for why the location is blocked or unavailable, such as maintenance, damage, safety hold, or quality quarantine.
Timestamp when the storage location record was first created in the WMS system.
Scheduled frequency for cycle counting inventory at this location to maintain inventory accuracy and compliance.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Configuration

description: Vertical level or shelf position within the bay for height-based slotting and equipment compatibility.
Indicates whether the location is designated for DSD operations where products bypass the DC and are delivered directly to retail stores.
Date when the storage location became active and available for warehouse operations.
Type of material handling equipment required to access this storage location for put-away and picking operations.
Date when the storage location is scheduled to be decommissioned or removed from active use. Null for indefinite locations.

business_glossary_term: First Expired First Out (FEFO) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether the location supports FEFO inventory rotation logic for expiry-sensitive products (pharmaceuticals, food, cosmetics).

business_glossary_term: First In First Out (FIFO) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether the location supports FIFO inventory rotation logic for age-based stock management.
Indicates whether the location is certified and equipped for storing hazardous materials per OSHA and EPA regulations.
Physical height dimension of the storage location in centimeters for vertical clearance and equipment reach validation.
Date when the most recent cycle count was performed at this storage location.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count History

description: Timestamp when the storage location record was most recently updated in the WMS system.
Physical length dimension of the storage location in centimeters for dimensional slotting and equipment compatibility.
Business identifier for the storage location as defined in Blue Yonder WMS. Typically formatted as aisle-bay-level-bin (e.g., A01-B05-L03-P12).
Human-readable name or description of the storage location for operational reference.
Current operational status of the storage location indicating availability for inventory placement and retrieval.
Classification of the storage location by operational function: bulk storage, active pick face, reserve inventory, staging area, dock door, or cross-dock zone.
Indicates whether the location permits storage of multiple lot or batch numbers for the same SKU or requires lot segregation.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Location Master, GMP Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Mixed Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) Allowed Flag
description: Indicates whether the location permits storage of multiple SKUs simultaneously or requires single-SKU dedication.
Indicates whether this location is designated as an active pick face for order fulfillment operations.
Order fulfillment picking method supported by this location: batch picking, wave picking, zone picking, discrete (single-order), or cluster picking.
Algorithm used to assign incoming inventory to this location: directed (system-assigned), random, fixed (dedicated SKU), or dynamic (velocity-based).
Priority ranking for automated replenishment from reserve to pick locations, with lower numbers indicating higher priority.
Temperature control classification for the storage location to ensure product integrity and regulatory compliance (ambient, refrigerated 2-8°C, frozen <-18°C, controlled room temperature).
Maximum volume capacity of the storage location in cubic meters for space utilization and slotting algorithms.
Maximum weight capacity of the storage location in kilograms for safe load management and slotting optimization.
Physical width dimension of the storage location in centimeters for dimensional slotting and equipment compatibility.
Logical zone classification within the distribution center for grouping locations by product category, velocity, or operational workflow (e.g., FAST-PICK, SLOW-MOVE, HAZMAT).
Unique identifier for the cycle count event record. Primary key for the distribution cycle count entity.
Identifier of the supervisor or manager who approved the cycle count adjustment.
Identifier of the distribution center where the cycle count was performed.
Identifier of the specific storage location (bin, rack, aisle) within the DC where the count was performed.
Identifier of the specific lot or batch being counted, critical for FEFO/FIFO inventory rotation and traceability.
Identifier of the warehouse associate who performed the physical count.
Identifier of the product SKU being counted in this cycle count line.
ABC inventory classification of the SKU at the time of count: A (high value/velocity), B (medium), C (low), D (obsolete/slow-moving).
Indicates whether the inventory adjustment has been approved by a supervisor or manager.
Indicates whether an inventory adjustment is required based on the variance exceeding tolerance thresholds.
The date and time when the cycle count adjustment was approved by a supervisor or manager.
The date and time when the physical counting activity was completed.
The method used to perform the physical count: manual (paper-based), RF scanner (handheld device), voice picking (voice-directed), or automated (RFID/sensor).
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Module

description: Business identifier for the cycle count event, typically generated by the WMS. Format: CC-YYYYMMDD-NNNN.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Module

description: The business reason triggering this cycle count: routine (scheduled ABC cycle), discrepancy (prior variance), audit (compliance), quality (QC hold), recall (product recall), transfer (location move).
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Module

description: The date and time when the physical counting activity began.
Current lifecycle status of the cycle count event.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Module

description: Classification of the cycle count event: scheduled (routine ABC cycle), ad-hoc (unplanned), exception (triggered by discrepancy), blind (counter does not see system quantity), or targeted (specific SKU/lot focus).
The actual physical quantity counted by the warehouse associate during the cycle count event.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Module

description: The date and time when this cycle count record was first created in the system.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the inventory value variance amount.
The expiration or best-before date of the lot/batch being counted, critical for FEFO inventory rotation.
The financial impact of the variance, calculated as variance_quantity multiplied by the standard cost of the SKU. Expressed in the DC's functional currency.
The date and time when this cycle count record was last updated in the system.
Sequential number indicating which recount iteration this represents (1 for first recount, 2 for second, etc.). Null if no recount performed.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Module

description: Indicates whether a recount is required due to significant variance or quality control procedures.
The date on which the cycle count was scheduled to be performed.
The inventory status of the counted stock: available (unrestricted), hold (QC hold), quarantine (quality review), damaged, expired, or reserved (allocated to orders).
The quantity of the SKU/lot recorded in the WMS at the time of the cycle count.
The acceptable variance percentage threshold. Variances within this percentage may not require adjustment.
The acceptable variance quantity threshold defined for this SKU/location combination. Variances within this threshold may not require adjustment.

The unit in which quantities are expressed: EA (each), CS (case), PL (pallet), LB (pound), KG (kilogram), L (liter), GAL (gallon). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|CS|PL|LB|KG|L|GAL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Free-text notes providing additional context or explanation for the variance observed during the cycle count.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Module

description: The variance expressed as a percentage of the system quantity, calculated as (variance_quantity / system_quantity) * 100.
The difference between counted quantity and system quantity (counted minus system). Positive indicates overage, negative indicates shortage.

Root cause classification for the variance: picking error, receiving error, damage, theft, system error, location error, expiry, or other. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: picking_error|receiving_error|damage|theft|system_error|location_error|expiry|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The unique transaction identifier generated by the WMS for this cycle count event, used for audit trail and system reconciliation.
Unique identifier for the inbound receipt transaction. Primary key for this entity.
Identifier of the transportation carrier that delivered the shipment to the distribution center.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Receiving operations incur expenses (labor, equipment) that are allocated to a cost center for expense tracking and budgeting.
Identifier of the distribution center facility where the goods were received.

Foreign key linking to manufacturing.manufacturing_facility. Business justification: Internal transfer receipt: inbound receipts from own plants need the source manufacturing facility to track internal logistics and cost allocation.
Identifier of the quality control personnel who performed the inspection, used for accountability and audit trail.

Foreign key linking to research.rd_project. Business justification: Required for R&D material receipt tracking; links each inbound receipt to the RD project that requested the raw material for formulation trials.
Identifier of the warehouse employee who processed the inbound receipt, used for labor tracking and accountability.
Identifier of the supplier or vendor who shipped the goods, representing the counterparty in this receipt transaction.
Identifier of the specific warehouse or storage facility within the distribution center where goods were received.
Quantity of goods accepted into inventory after quality inspection, excluding rejected or damaged items.
Precise date and time when the physical goods arrived and were checked in at the receiving dock, representing the principal business event for this transaction.
Reference to the Advanced Shipping Notice document sent by the supplier prior to shipment arrival, enabling pre-receipt planning and dock scheduling.
Number of cases or cartons received in this inbound shipment.
ISO standard container identifier for ocean freight shipments, following the BIC (Bureau International des Containers) format.
Date and time when this receipt record was first created in the system, representing the audit trail start point.
Indicator of whether any discrepancies (quantity, quality, or documentation) were identified during the receiving process.
Free-text description providing additional details about any discrepancies identified during the receiving process.
Classification of the type of discrepancy identified during receiving, used for root cause analysis and supplier performance management.
Physical dock door location where the inbound shipment was unloaded, used for labor planning and dock utilization tracking.
Total quantity of goods expected to be received based on the ASN or purchase order, used for discrepancy detection.
SAP Material Management (MM) goods receipt document number generated upon posting the receipt to inventory, linking WMS to ERP.
Date and time when this receipt record was last updated, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.

business_glossary_term: On Time In Full (OTIF) Compliant Flag
description: Indicator of whether this receipt met both on-time delivery and complete quantity requirements, key supplier performance metric.
Number of pallets received in this inbound shipment, used for dock capacity planning and labor allocation.
Reference to the originating purchase order that authorized this inbound shipment.
Date and time when all received goods were moved from the receiving dock to their designated storage locations, completing the inbound process.
Indicator of whether formal quality inspection was required for this receipt based on product category, supplier risk profile, or regulatory requirements.
Current status of the quality inspection process for this receipt, tracking progression through quality control workflow.
Date and time when all receiving activities (unloading, inspection, put-away) were completed and the receipt was closed in the WMS.
Externally-known business identifier for the inbound receipt, used for tracking and reference across systems and with suppliers.
Current lifecycle status of the inbound receipt transaction, tracking progression from scheduling through completion or exception handling.
Classification of the inbound receipt based on the source and nature of the goods being received.
Actual total quantity of goods physically received and counted during the receiving process.
Quantity of goods rejected during receiving due to quality issues, damage, or non-conformance to specifications.
Planned date for the inbound shipment to arrive at the distribution center, based on ASN or supplier commitment.
Indicator of whether the security seal was found intact upon arrival, critical for quality control and loss prevention.
Security seal identifier applied to the trailer or container, verified upon receipt to ensure shipment integrity and prevent tampering.
Indicator of whether temperature verification was required for this receipt due to cold chain or temperature-sensitive product requirements.
Indicator of whether the recorded temperature was within acceptable range per product specifications and cold chain requirements.
Actual temperature reading in Celsius recorded during receipt inspection for temperature-sensitive products, critical for cold chain compliance.
Unique identifier of the trailer or truck that delivered the shipment, used for tracking and carrier performance analysis.

Standard unit of measure for the quantities recorded in this receipt (Each, Case, Pallet, Kilogram, Pound, Liter, Gallon). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|CS|PL|EA|KG|LB|LT|GL — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Unique identifier for the inbound receipt line. Primary key for this entity.
User ID of the warehouse associate who physically received and recorded this line. Used for accountability and performance tracking.
Reference to the parent inbound receipt header transaction. Links this line to the overall receipt event.

Foreign key linking to research.rd_project. Business justification: Needed to associate each receipt line (specific SKU/lot) with the RD project using it, enabling traceability of trial material consumption.

Foreign key linking to regulatory.registration. Business justification: Regulatory registration verification during inbound receipt ensures each received SKU is registered in the jurisdiction, a standard compliance step.
Foreign key linking to product.sku. Business justification: Link receipt line to SKU master for traceability and quality inspection; required by receipt processing and compliance audit reports.
Foreign key linking to inventory.stock_position. Business justification: RECEIVING: When a receipt line is processed, a Stock Position record is created/updated to reflect on‑hand quantity at the DC.
Reference to the supplier or vendor who shipped the goods. Used for supplier performance tracking and procurement analytics.
Line number within the ASN document corresponding to this receipt line. Enables automated matching between ASN and physical receipt.
Advanced Shipping Notice document number sent by the supplier prior to shipment arrival. Used for pre-receipt planning and variance detection.
Quality condition assessment of the received goods. Determines whether product can be put away into available inventory or requires special handling.
Date and time when this receipt line record was first created in the warehouse management system. Audit trail for data lineage.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the unit cost and extended cost. Supports multi-currency procurement operations.
Free-text description of any damage, defects, or quality issues observed during receipt inspection. Used for claims and supplier performance tracking.
Expected quantity in cases as specified in the Advanced Shipping Notice (ASN) or purchase order. Used for variance detection.
Expected quantity in eaches as specified in the Advanced Shipping Notice (ASN) or purchase order. Used for variance detection.
Date when the product expires and can no longer be sold or used. Critical for FEFO rotation and inventory management in consumer goods.
Total cost for this receipt line calculated as unit cost multiplied by received quantity. Used for inventory valuation and financial reconciliation.
Global Trade Item Number uniquely identifying the product in the supply chain. May be GTIN-8, GTIN-12, GTIN-13, or GTIN-14 format.
Date and time when this receipt line record was last updated. Audit trail for tracking changes to receipt data.
Sequential line number within the inbound receipt. Used for ordering and referencing specific lines in the receipt document.
Manufacturing lot or batch number assigned by the supplier. Critical for traceability, quality control, and recall management in consumer goods.
Date when the product was manufactured by the supplier. Used for shelf-life calculations and FEFO inventory rotation.
Unique identifier for the pallet or handling unit containing this receipt line. Used for put-away and storage location assignment.
reference: GS1 SSCC Standard, Blue Yonder WMS

description: Line number on the purchase order corresponding to this receipt line. Enables three-way matching between PO, receipt, and invoice.
Purchase order number authorizing the receipt of these goods. Links the receipt to the original procurement transaction.
Date and time when the goods were put away into their assigned storage location. Used for warehouse productivity and cycle time measurement.
Indicates whether this receipt line requires quality inspection before being released to available inventory. True for regulated or high-risk products.
Status of quality inspection for this receipt line. Determines whether goods can be released to available inventory or must remain in quarantine.
Current processing status of this receipt line within the warehouse workflow. Tracks progression from initial receipt through put-away completion.
Quantity of product received measured in cases. Represents the outer packaging unit typically used for warehouse handling.
Quantity of product received measured in individual units (eaches). Represents the consumer-facing unit count.
Date and time when the goods were physically received at the warehouse dock. Critical for OTIF performance measurement and cycle time analytics.
18-digit Serial Shipping Container Code identifying the logistics unit. Global standard for tracking pallets and containers in the supply chain.
Warehouse storage location code where the received goods were put away. Identifies the bin, rack, or zone within the distribution center.
Temperature measurement in Celsius recorded at the time of receipt. Critical for cold chain compliance and product quality verification.
reference: Cold Chain Standards, FDA CFR Title 21

description: Cost per unit for the received goods as specified in the purchase order. Used for inventory valuation and COGS calculation.
Primary unit of measure for the received quantity. Defines the counting and handling unit for warehouse operations.
Universal Product Code barcode identifier for the received item. Standard 12-digit UPC-A format used in North American retail.
Difference between expected and received quantity in cases. Positive values indicate overages, negative values indicate shortages.
Difference between expected and received quantity in eaches. Positive values indicate overages, negative values indicate shortages.
Code identifying the distribution center or warehouse facility where the receipt occurred. Used for multi-site inventory management.
Primary key for inventory_position

Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business justification: Inventory compliance reporting links each inventory position to its applicable regulatory obligation to track deadlines and status.
Identifier of the distribution center where the inventory is physically located.

business_glossary_term: Storage Location Dc Location Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to distribution.distribution_storage_location. Business justification: Inventory position records on‑hand quantities at a specific DC location. Linking to distribution_storage_location provides the authoritative location details and removes the generic storage_location_i

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Supports Inventory Ownership Dashboard, assigning a responsible employee for each DC inventory position for accountability and cycle‑count oversight.
Identifier of the specific lot or batch of the SKU. Critical for traceability, quality control, and FEFO inventory rotation.
Foreign key linking to research.rd_project. Business justification: Provides real‑time visibility of prototype SKU inventory tied to the RD project, essential for launch readiness dashboards.
Identifier of the product SKU for which inventory position is tracked.
The actual measured weight of the inventory for catch weight items. Used for billing and compliance when item weight varies.
Indicates whether the SKU is a catch weight item requiring actual weight capture at transaction time (true) or standard weight (false).
The unit cost of the inventory lot. Used for inventory valuation and cost of goods sold calculations. Business confidential financial data.
The timestamp when this inventory position record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for inventory valuation (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
The number of days the inventory has been on hand since receipt. Calculated as current date minus receipt date. Used for aging analysis.
The number of days remaining until the inventory lot expires. Calculated as expiry date minus current date. Critical for FEFO rotation and markdown decisions.
The date on which the product lot expires and can no longer be sold or distributed. Critical for FEFO inventory management and regulatory compliance.

description: The physical condition classification of the inventory. Used for disposition decisions and channel restrictions.
The current operational status of the inventory position. Determines availability for picking and order fulfillment.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Inventory Status Codes

description: The date when this inventory position was last physically counted during a cycle count operation. Used to schedule next count and assess inventory accuracy.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Cycle Count Management

description: The date when inventory was last moved into or out of this storage location. Used for slow-moving inventory identification.

The type of the last inventory movement transaction that affected this position (receipt, putaway, pick, replenishment, transfer, adjustment, return). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: receipt|putaway|pick|replenishment|transfer|adjustment|return — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The timestamp when this inventory position record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data freshness assessment.
The warehouse management system license plate number assigned to the handling unit. Used for tracking and automated material handling.
The alphanumeric lot or batch number assigned during manufacturing. Used for traceability and recall management.
The date on which the product lot was manufactured. Used for shelf-life calculations and FEFO rotation.
Indicates the ownership model of the inventory (owned by company, consignment from supplier, customer-owned for returns, vendor-managed inventory).
The unique identifier of the pallet or handling unit on which the inventory is stored. Used for warehouse automation and tracking.
Indicates whether this inventory position is in a primary pick face location (true) or reserve storage (false). Pick face locations are optimized for order picking efficiency.
The date when the inventory was put away into this storage location after receiving. Used for aging analysis and FEFO compliance.
The quantity of on-hand inventory that has been allocated to outbound orders or reservations but not yet picked. Reduces available-to-pick quantity.
The quantity available for new order allocation and picking. Calculated as quantity_on_hand minus quantity_allocated minus quantity_quarantine minus quantity_hold.
reference: SAP S/4HANA ATP Logic, Blue Yonder WMS

description: The quantity of inventory identified as damaged and not suitable for sale or distribution. Typically awaiting disposal or return to supplier.
The quantity of inventory placed on hold due to quality issues, customer complaints, or pending investigation. Not available for picking.
The total physical quantity of the SKU-lot currently present in the storage location. Measured in the SKU's base unit of measure.
The quantity of inventory placed in quarantine status pending quality inspection or regulatory clearance. Not available for picking.
The quantity of inventory reserved for specific customers, channels, or promotional programs. Subset of allocated quantity with additional business constraints.
The date when the inventory lot was received into the distribution center. Used for inventory aging and supplier performance tracking.
Indicates whether this inventory position requires replenishment from reserve to pick face (true) or not (false). Triggers automated replenishment tasks.
The timestamp when this inventory position snapshot was captured. Used for point-in-time inventory reporting and trend analysis.
The logical zone within the distribution center where the inventory is stored (e.g., ambient, refrigerated, frozen, hazmat, high-velocity, reserve).
The temperature control zone classification for the storage location. Critical for cold chain compliance and product quality.

Number of days advance notice required to terminate the VMI agreement by either party.
Unique identifier for the out-of-stock event record.
Identifier of the warehouse, distribution center, or retail location where the OOS event occurred.
Reference to the previous OOS event ID for the same SKU-location if this is a recurrence, enabling trend analysis.

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Out‑of‑stock events are owned by a specific employee who drives corrective actions; required for OOS root‑cause analysis and SLA reporting.
Identifier of the SKU that experienced the out-of-stock condition.
Actual observed demand in units during the OOS event period, used to identify demand spikes or forecast misses.
Brand name of the SKU that experienced the OOS event, used for brand-level OOS performance tracking.
Distribution channel type where the OOS event occurred: retail, wholesale, e-commerce, DSD (Direct Store Delivery), or DTC (Direct to Consumer).
Description of the corrective action plan implemented to prevent recurrence of similar OOS events in the future.
Timestamp when the OOS event record was first created in the system.
Boolean flag indicating whether the OOS event resulted in direct customer impact such as lost sales, customer complaints, or service level breaches.
Forecasted demand in units for the period during which the OOS event occurred, used to compare actual vs. planned demand.
System or channel that detected and reported the out-of-stock event, such as POS system, WMS, demand sensing platform, manual report, retail execution app, or EDI feed.
Estimated monetary value of sales lost due to the out-of-stock condition, calculated based on historical demand patterns and average selling price.
Estimated quantity of units that could not be sold due to the out-of-stock condition.
Current lifecycle status of the OOS event record: open (active OOS), resolved (inventory restored), under investigation (root cause analysis in progress), or closed (fully resolved and documented).
Forecast accuracy percentage for the SKU-location during the period of the OOS event, calculated as (1 - |actual - forecast| / actual) * 100.
Severity classification of the OOS event impact based on lost sales value, SKU importance, and customer impact. Categories: critical, high, medium, low.
System-recorded inventory quantity on hand at the time the OOS event was detected, used to identify phantom inventory situations.
Date of the most recent replenishment delivery prior to the OOS event, used to analyze replenishment frequency adequacy.
Timestamp when the OOS event record was most recently updated, reflecting changes to status, resolution actions, or root cause analysis.
Date of the next scheduled replenishment delivery at the time of the OOS event, used to assess replenishment planning gaps.
Total duration of the out-of-stock event measured in hours, calculated as the difference between end and start timestamps.
Timestamp when the out-of-stock condition was resolved and inventory became available again.
Timestamp when the out-of-stock condition was first detected. Sourced from POS data feeds or demand sensing signals.

Classification of the OOS event type: warehouse stockout (no inventory in facility), shelf stockout (inventory in back room but not on shelf), phantom inventory (system shows stock but physical count is zero), or system mismatch.
Actual on-shelf availability percentage achieved during the period including the OOS event, calculated from POS and inventory data.
Target on-shelf availability percentage for the SKU-location at the time of the OOS event, used to measure performance against goals.
Product category classification of the SKU that experienced the OOS event, used for category-level OOS analysis and reporting.
Boolean flag indicating whether this OOS event is a recurrence of a previous OOS event for the same SKU-location combination within a defined time window.
Configured reorder point threshold for the SKU at this location, used to evaluate whether replenishment triggers were properly set.
Action taken to resolve the out-of-stock event, such as emergency replenishment, transfer from alternate location, expedited shipment, customer backorder, substitution offered, or no action taken.
Timestamp when the resolution action was initiated or completed to address the out-of-stock condition.
Primary root cause classification for the OOS event. Categories include demand spike, replenishment failure, forecast miss, upstream stockout, logistics delay, or system error.
Detailed narrative explanation of the root cause behind the out-of-stock event, providing context beyond the category classification.
Configured safety stock level for the SKU at this location at the time of the OOS event, used to assess whether safety stock was breached.
Boolean flag indicating whether the OOS event caused a breach of service level agreement commitments to customers or retail partners.
Unique identifier for the stock movement transaction. Primary key for the stock movement record.

Foreign key linking to product.bom_line. Business justification: Manufacturing consumption tracking links inventory movements to specific BOM lines, enabling component usage analysis per product in the Component Consumption Report.

Foreign key linking to marketing.campaign_flight. Business justification: Logistics teams track stock movements tied to specific campaign flights to measure promotional material delivery and OTIF performance.
Transportation carrier responsible for moving inventory between locations for inter-node transfers.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Cost accounting for each inventory movement requires linking to the responsible cost center for internal reporting and allocation.
Warehouse, plant, or storage location to which inventory is being moved. Null for goods issues to external destinations.
System user ID of the person who posted or recorded this stock movement for audit trail and accountability.
Reference to the logistics shipment for inter-plant or inter-warehouse transfers to track in-transit inventory.
Foreign key linking to sales.order. Business justification: Needed to tie inventory movements to the originating sales order for order fulfillment audit and cost of goods sold reconciliation.
Warehouse, plant, or storage location from which inventory is being moved. Null for goods receipts from external sources.
Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Profitability analysis of inventory flows assigns each movement to a profit center, needed for segment reporting.

Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: REQUIRED: PO receipt tracking for OTIF reporting and financial reconciliation links stock movements to the originating purchase order.
Reference to the original stock movement record that this transaction reverses or cancels.
Reference to the SKU involved in this stock movement event.
Supplier or vendor from whom goods were received for goods receipt movements.
Customer to whom goods were issued for sales order fulfillment or Direct to Consumer (DTC) shipments.
Manufacturing batch or lot number for traceability and recall readiness. Critical for FEFO/FIFO rotation and quality control.
reference: ISO 22716 GMP for Cosmetics, FDA 21 CFR Part 11

description: Timestamp when this stock movement record was first created in the system for audit trail.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the movement value (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
Date on the source document (purchase order, production order, delivery note) that triggered this movement.
Shelf life expiration date for perishable or time-sensitive products. Critical for First Expired First Out (FEFO) rotation and Out of Stock (OOS) prevention.
Timestamp when this stock movement record was last updated or modified for change tracking.
Date when the product was manufactured or produced. Used for shelf life calculation and traceability.
reference: ISO 22716 GMP for Cosmetics, FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: SAP material document number generated for this goods movement. Unique identifier in the source ERP system.
Fiscal year of the material document for SAP document key uniqueness.
High-level classification of the movement event for reporting and analytics purposes.
Free-text notes or comments providing additional context about the stock movement event.
Precise date and time when the physical inventory movement occurred or was recorded in the system.

SAP movement type code identifying the nature of the inventory transaction (e.g., 101=Goods Receipt from PO, 261=Goods Issue to Production, 311=Stock Transfer, 551=Scrapping, 601=Goods Receipt from Delivery).
Manufacturing plant or distribution center code where the movement occurred.
Date when the stock movement was posted to the inventory ledger for financial and inventory accounting purposes.
Indicates whether this stock movement requires quality inspection before the inventory can be released for use.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management, SAP S/4HANA QM

description: Quantity of inventory moved in this transaction. Positive for receipts/increases, negative for issues/decreases.
Code explaining the business reason for the movement (e.g., quality issue, damage, expiration, customer return, production scrap).
Line item number within the reference document that corresponds to this stock movement.
Document number of the source transaction (PO number, production order number, delivery note number) that triggered this movement.

Type of source document that initiated this stock movement for audit trail and reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: purchase_order|production_order|sales_order|delivery_note|transfer_order|return_order|adjustment_document — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Flag indicating whether this movement is a reversal or cancellation of a previous stock movement transaction.
Unique serial number for serialized inventory items requiring individual unit tracking.
reference: GS1 SGTIN (Serialized Global Trade Item Number)

description: SAP special stock type indicator (e.g., E=Sales Order Stock, K=Consignment Stock, O=Project Stock, W=Vendor Managed Inventory).
Classification of inventory status determining availability for use (unrestricted=available for sale/use, quality_inspection=pending QC, blocked=not available).
Specific storage location or bin within the plant or warehouse where inventory is stored.
Total financial value of the inventory movement (quantity × unit cost) for financial reporting and inventory accounting.
reference: GAAP Inventory Valuation, SAP S/4HANA FI

description: Cost per unit of inventory at the time of movement for inventory valuation and Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) calculation.
reference: GAAP Inventory Valuation, SAP S/4HANA FI

description: Unit of measure for the movement quantity (e.g., EA=Each, CS=Case, KG=Kilogram, LT=Liter).
Sub-classification for split valuation of the same material (e.g., domestic vs imported, new vs refurbished).

Unique surrogate identifier for the transportation carrier record in the Consumer Goods logistics master data. Primary key for all carrier-related references across shipments, freight orders, contracts, and invoices.
reference: GS1 GLN Standards; SAP S/4HANA TM Carrier Master

description: Foreign key linking to sustainability.esg_commitment. Business justification: Corporate policy tracks carrier ESG commitments to ensure supplier compliance and include them in carrier performance scorecards.

Reference to the corresponding vendor/supplier master record in the ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle Cloud ERP) for this carrier. Links the carrier master to the procurement and accounts payable vendor record for freight invoice processing and payment.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master (LFA1); Oracle Cloud Procurement Supplier

description: Indicates whether the carrier provides a real-time shipment tracking API for track-and-trace integration. Enables automated shipment status updates in the TMS without manual EDI 214 processing. Used in carrier technology capability assessment.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Integration Framework; SAP S/4HANA TM Track and Trace

description: Current lifecycle status of the carrier in the Consumer Goods approved carrier program. Active carriers are eligible for shipment tendering. Suspended carriers are temporarily blocked pending compliance review. Blacklisted carriers are permanently disqualified. Drives carrier selection eligibility in TMS routing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA TM Carrier Status; FMCSA Compliance Review

description: Primary transportation mode classification of the carrier. Drives rate card selection, shipment planning rules, and EDI transaction sets. TL (Truckload), LTL (Less-Than-Truckload), parcel, rail, ocean, air, intermodal, and courier are the standard classifications in consumer goods logistics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: truckload|less_than_truckload|parcel|rail|ocean|air|intermodal|courier — promote to reference product]
reference: GS1 Transport Mode Codes; SAP S/4HANA TM Carrier Type; Blue Yonder WMS Carrier Classification

description: Indicates whether the carrier has certified temperature-controlled transportation capability (refrigerated or frozen) for cold-chain compliant shipments of health, hygiene, and personal care products requiring temperature management. Critical for product safety and regulatory compliance.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211; ISO 9001 Quality Management; GDP (Good Distribution Practice) Guidelines

description: Expiry date of the current master transportation services agreement. Triggers contract renewal workflows and rate renegotiation processes. Shipment tendering to the carrier may be restricted after this date if no renewal is in place.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Contract Management; Oracle Cloud Procurement Contracts

description: Effective start date of the current master transportation services agreement between Consumer Goods and the carrier. Defines the period during which contracted rates and service commitments are valid.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Contract Management; Oracle Cloud Procurement Contracts

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code where the carrier is legally registered and incorporated. Used for cross-border compliance checks, customs documentation, and carrier eligibility for specific trade lanes.

Timestamp when the carrier master record was first created in the Consumer Goods logistics data platform. Provides audit trail for record provenance and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOX IT General Controls; ISO 9001 Record Management; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which freight rates and invoices are denominated for this carrier. Used in multi-currency freight cost management, FX conversion, and financial reporting.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA FI Currency Configuration; SOX Financial Reporting

description: Unique identifier assigned by the U.S. Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) to commercial motor carriers operating in interstate commerce. Required for regulatory compliance verification and safety rating lookup. Mandatory for US-based trucking carriers.
reference: FMCSA 49 CFR Part 390; U.S. DOT Registration

description: Nine-digit Dun & Bradstreet Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number uniquely identifying the carrier's business entity globally. Used for supplier risk assessment, credit verification, and EDI trading partner identification.
reference: Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Registry; GS1 GLN Standards; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Master

description: Indicates whether the carrier supports Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) for automated exchange of shipment tenders (204), load tenders (990), shipment status (214), and freight invoices (210). EDI-capable carriers are preferred for high-volume automated tendering in the TMS.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 EDI Standards; GS1 EDI Guidelines; SAP S/4HANA TM EDI Configuration

description: Carrier's EDI interchange identifier used in the ISA segment of X12 EDI transactions. Combined with the EDI qualifier, this uniquely identifies the carrier as an EDI trading partner. Required for automated tender and status message routing.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA Segment Specification; SAP S/4HANA TM EDI Partner Profile

description: Two-digit qualifier code identifying the type of EDI sender/receiver identifier used in ISA segment of X12 EDI transactions (e.g., 02 = DUNS, 08 = UCC/EAN, ZZ = Mutually Defined). Required for EDI trading partner setup and message routing.
reference: ANSI ASC X12 ISA Segment Specification; GS1 EDI Standards

description: Date on which the current FMCSA safety rating was issued or last updated. Used to assess rating currency and trigger re-evaluation workflows when ratings are older than the compliance review threshold.
reference: FMCSA 49 CFR Part 385; FMCSA Safety Measurement System (SMS)

business_glossary_term: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) Safety Rating
description: Official safety fitness rating assigned by the FMCSA to motor carriers based on compliance reviews and safety audits. Satisfactory rating is required for carrier approval in Consumer Goods' carrier program. Conditional or Unsatisfactory ratings trigger carrier review or suspension. Mandatory compliance field for US trucking carriers.
reference: FMCSA 49 CFR Part 385; FMCSA Safety Measurement System (SMS)

description: Description of the carrier's operational geographic coverage scope, including regions, countries, or trade lanes served. Used in TMS routing logic to filter eligible carriers by origin-destination pair. Examples: 'Continental US', 'US-Canada cross-border', 'Trans-Pacific', 'EU domestic'.
reference: SAP S/4HANA TM Transportation Lane; Blue Yonder WMS Carrier Zone Configuration

description: Expiry date of the carrier's hazardous materials transportation certification. Triggers compliance alerts and blocks HAZMAT shipment tendering to the carrier if certification has lapsed.
reference: DOT 49 CFR Parts 171-180; FMCSA HAZMAT Registration

description: Indicates whether the carrier holds valid certification to transport hazardous materials (HAZMAT) as defined by DOT 49 CFR. Required for shipments of aerosols, flammable products, and chemical-based consumer goods. Validated against DOT HAZMAT registration database.
reference: DOT 49 CFR Parts 171-180; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200; EPA RCRA

description: Full street address of the carrier's principal place of business or corporate headquarters. Used for legal correspondence, contract execution, and regulatory filings. Includes street, city, state/province, postal code, and country.
reference: FMCSA Carrier Registration; GDPR Article 4; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Master Address

business_glossary_term: International Air Transport Association (IATA) Carrier Code
description: 2-3 character alphanumeric code assigned by IATA to identify air freight carriers. Used for air waybill generation, air freight booking, and international air cargo tracking. Applicable only to air freight carriers.
reference: IATA Resolution 762; IATA Airline Coding Directory

description: Maximum coverage amount (in USD) of the carrier's cargo insurance policy covering loss or damage to goods in transit. Consumer Goods mandates minimum cargo insurance thresholds based on shipment value profiles. Critical for high-value CPG product shipments.
reference: FMCSA 49 CFR Part 387; ISO 9001 Supplier Qualification

description: Reference number of the carrier's current certificate of insurance (COI) on file with Consumer Goods. Used for insurance verification, claims processing, and audit trail of carrier compliance documentation.
reference: FMCSA 49 CFR Part 387; ISO 9001 Document Control

description: Date on which the carrier's insurance certificate expires. Triggers automated renewal reminder workflows and carrier status suspension if insurance lapses. Critical compliance field for carrier program management.
reference: FMCSA 49 CFR Part 387; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Certificate Management

description: Maximum coverage amount (in USD) of the carrier's general liability insurance policy. Consumer Goods requires minimum liability coverage thresholds as a condition of carrier approval. Validated during carrier onboarding and annual renewal.
reference: FMCSA 49 CFR Part 387; ISO 9001 Supplier Qualification; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Evaluation

description: Date of the most recent compliance review conducted for this carrier, covering safety ratings, insurance certificates, HAZMAT certifications, and contractual obligations. Used to schedule periodic re-evaluations and flag overdue reviews.
reference: FMCSA Safety Measurement System; ISO 9001 Supplier Audit; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Evaluation

description: Full legal registered business name of the transportation carrier as filed with regulatory authorities (FMCSA, state business registry). Used in contracts, freight invoices, and regulatory filings. Must match the name on the carrier's operating authority.
reference: FMCSA Carrier Registration; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Master (LFA1)

description: Maximum weight capacity in kilograms that the carrier's standard equipment can transport per shipment. Used in load planning, shipment consolidation, and carrier eligibility checks to prevent overweight violations.
reference: DOT 49 CFR Part 395; SAP S/4HANA TM Capacity Management; Blue Yonder WMS Load Planning

description: Operating authority number issued by the FMCSA to for-hire motor carriers transporting regulated commodities in interstate commerce. Distinct from DOT number — MC number grants operating authority while DOT number is for safety registration. Used in carrier compliance validation.
reference: FMCSA 49 CFR Part 365; FMCSA Operating Authority

description: Date on which the carrier was formally approved and onboarded into Consumer Goods' carrier program, completing all compliance checks, insurance verification, and EDI/API setup. Marks the start of the carrier's operational eligibility.
reference: SAP S/4HANA TM Carrier Onboarding; ISO 9001 Supplier Qualification

description: Contractual payment terms agreed with the carrier for freight invoice settlement. Drives accounts payable scheduling and cash flow planning. Standard terms in consumer goods logistics range from Net 15 to Net 60 days.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Payment Terms; Oracle Cloud Financials AP; SOX Financial Controls

description: Indicates whether the carrier has been designated as a preferred carrier in Consumer Goods' carrier program, typically based on negotiated rates, service performance, and strategic partnership status. Preferred carriers receive priority in TMS automated tendering sequences.
reference: SAP S/4HANA TM Carrier Selection; Blue Yonder WMS Carrier Preference

description: Business email address of the primary carrier contact for operational communications, tender notifications, and account management. Used in EDI onboarding and carrier portal access provisioning.
reference: GDPR Article 4; SAP S/4HANA Vendor Contact; Blue Yonder WMS Carrier Profile

description: Full name of the primary business contact at the carrier organization responsible for account management, contract negotiations, and escalation handling. Used in carrier relationship management and communication workflows.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Vendor Contact; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud Account Management

description: Primary business telephone number for the carrier contact, used for operational coordination, shipment tracking inquiries, and exception management. Formatted per E.164 international standard.
reference: GDPR Article 4; ITU-T E.164 Telephone Numbering

description: Unique 2-4 character alpha code assigned by the National Motor Freight Traffic Association (NMFTA) to identify transportation carriers in North America. Used in EDI transactions (204, 214, 990) and freight billing. Mandatory for motor carriers operating in the US.
reference: NMFTA SCAC Registry; ANSI ASC X12 EDI Standards

description: Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes representing the countries in which the carrier provides transportation services. Used for international shipment routing, customs compliance validation, and carrier eligibility filtering in cross-border logistics.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; GS1 Country Codes; SAP S/4HANA TM Transportation Lane

description: Service level classification offered by the carrier indicating transit speed and handling commitment. Drives SLA assignment, freight cost tier selection, and shipment routing logic in the TMS. Used in OTIF (On Time In Full) performance measurement.
reference: SAP S/4HANA TM Shipping Conditions; Blue Yonder WMS Service Level

description: Federal tax identification number (EIN/TIN) or VAT registration number of the carrier, used for tax compliance, 1099 reporting, and cross-border customs documentation. Required for freight invoice processing and IRS reporting.
reference: IRS Publication 1220; SOX Tax Compliance; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC

description: Maximum temperature (in degrees Celsius) that the carrier's cold-chain equipment can maintain during transit. Combined with the minimum temperature range, defines the carrier's certified temperature corridor for cold-chain shipments.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211; ISO 22716 GMP for Cosmetics; GDP Guidelines

description: Minimum temperature (in degrees Celsius) that the carrier's cold-chain equipment can maintain during transit. Used to validate carrier eligibility for temperature-sensitive product shipments and cold-chain compliance verification.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211; ISO 22716 GMP for Cosmetics; GDP Guidelines

description: URL template for the carrier's web-based shipment tracking portal, with a placeholder (e.g., {tracking_number}) for dynamic substitution. Used to generate direct tracking links in shipment notifications, customer portals, and internal TMS dashboards.
reference: Blue Yonder WMS Carrier Integration; SAP S/4HANA TM Track and Trace

description: Doing-business-as (DBA) or trade name used by the carrier in commercial operations, which may differ from the legal registered name. Used in operational communications, carrier portals, and reporting where the trade name is more recognizable.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Vendor Master; Blue Yonder TMS Carrier Profile

description: Unique system-generated surrogate identifier for the carrier contract record in the logistics data platform. Primary key for the carrier_contract entity.
reference: GS1 Global Standards; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: Reference to the carrier (transportation service provider) party who is the counterparty to this freight contract. Links to the carrier master record.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD/MM Vendor Master; GS1 GLN Standard

description: Name or employee identifier of the logistics or procurement team member responsible for managing and maintaining this carrier contract. Used for contract governance, renewal notifications, and escalation routing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Purchasing Group; Oracle Cloud Procurement Buyer Assignment

description: Reference code identifying the accessorial charge schedule applicable to this contract. Accessorial charges include liftgate, residential delivery, inside delivery, detention, layover, hazmat handling, and temperature-controlled surcharges. Links to the accessorial rate table for freight audit and cost estimation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Accessorial Condition Records; NMFC Accessorial Definitions

description: Date on which the carrier contract was formally approved by the authorized approver. Used in contract governance, SOX audit trails, and procurement compliance reporting.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; Oracle Cloud Procurement Approval Workflow; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: Name or employee identifier of the authorized approver who signed off on this carrier contract. Required for SOX financial controls compliance and procurement governance. Supports audit trail for contract authorization.
reference: SOX Section 302/404 Internal Controls; Oracle Cloud Procurement Approval Workflow

description: Indicates whether this carrier contract automatically renews at expiry unless terminated with advance notice. When true, the renewal_notice_days field defines the required notice period. Supports contract lifecycle management and procurement planning.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Contract Management; Oracle Cloud Procurement

description: The primary negotiated freight rate under this contract before surcharges and accessorial charges are applied. The unit of measure for this rate is defined by the rate_type field (e.g., per mile, per CWT, per pallet, flat). Used as the foundation for freight cost estimation and freight audit rate lookup.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Freight Condition Records; Oracle Cloud Procurement

description: Frequency at which the carrier submits freight invoices under this contract. Per-shipment billing generates an invoice for each delivery; weekly/bi-weekly/monthly billing consolidates charges into periodic invoices. Impacts freight audit workflow and accounts payable processing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Invoice Processing; Oracle Cloud AP; EDI X12 210 Freight Invoice

description: Indicates whether this contract covers temperature-controlled (cold chain) shipments requiring refrigerated or frozen transport. When true, cold chain compliance monitoring, temperature logging, and FEFO inventory management protocols apply. Relevant for health, hygiene, and perishable consumer goods.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211 (Cold Chain); ISO 9001 Quality Management; FSMA

description: Externally-known, human-readable contract reference number assigned by the procurement or logistics team. Used in EDI communications, freight audit, and carrier correspondence. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA MM contract document number.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; EDI X12 Standard

description: Current lifecycle state of the carrier contract. Draft indicates contract is being authored; pending_approval is awaiting sign-off; active means the contract is in force; suspended means temporarily halted; expired means the term has lapsed; terminated means the contract was ended before expiry.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Contract Lifecycle; Oracle Cloud Procurement

description: Classification of the freight contract by commercial arrangement type. Spot contracts cover single-shipment rates; committed contracts lock volume at negotiated rates; preferred carrier agreements define priority tender; dedicated contracts reserve capacity; intermodal covers multi-mode arrangements; 3PL master covers third-party logistics umbrella agreements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Outline Agreement Types; Blue Yonder WMS

description: Timestamp when this carrier contract record was first created in the logistics data platform. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
reference: ISO 8601; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all rates, charges, and financial commitments under this contract are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency freight cost management and financial reporting.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SOX Financial Reporting

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the destination country covered by this contract. Used for cross-border freight classification, customs compliance, and international rate applicability.

Geographic destination zone or region covered by this contract for lane-level rate applicability. May represent a state, ZIP zone, city cluster, or carrier-defined zone code. Used in freight cost estimation and tender evaluation.
reference: GS1 GLN; SAP S/4HANA SD Transportation Zones

description: Number of hours the carrier's equipment (trailer/container) may remain at a Consumer Goods facility for loading or unloading without incurring detention charges. Exceeding this threshold triggers accessorial detention fees per the contract rate schedule.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Detention Condition Types; NMFC Detention Standards

description: Indicates whether the carrier supports EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) for automated tender, shipment status, and invoice exchange under this contract. EDI-capable carriers enable automated load tendering (EDI 204), shipment status updates (EDI 214), and freight invoice processing (EDI 210).
reference: EDI X12 Standards (204, 210, 214); GS1 EDI Standards

description: The date on which the carrier contract becomes legally binding and rates become applicable for freight tendering and cost estimation. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA MM contract validity start date.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; UCC Article 2 Contract Law

description: The date on which the carrier contract ceases to be valid and rates are no longer applicable. Nullable for evergreen contracts with no fixed end date. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA MM contract validity end date.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module; UCC Article 2 Contract Law

description: Defines how the fuel surcharge is calculated and applied: as a percentage of the base freight rate, a flat amount per mile, a flat amount per shipment, or dynamically linked to the DOE diesel fuel price index. Determines the fuel surcharge computation method in freight audit.
reference: DOE Diesel Fuel Index; SAP S/4HANA SD Condition Calculation Types

description: Contracted fuel surcharge rate expressed as a percentage of the base rate or as a fixed amount per unit, applied on top of the base freight rate to account for fuel cost variability. Linked to a fuel index table or DOE diesel price index. Critical for freight cost estimation and audit.
reference: DOE (U.S. Department of Energy) Diesel Fuel Index; SAP S/4HANA SD Surcharge Conditions

description: Indicates whether the carrier is certified and authorized under this contract to transport hazardous materials (hazmat) including flammable, corrosive, or toxic consumer goods ingredients. When true, DOT/IATA hazmat compliance documentation is required.
reference: DOT 49 CFR Hazardous Materials Regulations; IATA DGR; EPA RCRA

description: Maximum cargo insurance coverage amount provided by the carrier under this contract, expressed in the contract currency. Defines the financial liability limit for cargo loss or damage claims. Used in risk management and claims processing.
reference: Carmack Amendment (49 U.S.C. § 14706); CPSC; Oracle Cloud Financials

description: Contractual carrier liability limit per kilogram of cargo for loss or damage claims, expressed in the contract currency. Used in freight claims management to calculate maximum recoverable amounts for damaged or lost shipments.
reference: Carmack Amendment (49 U.S.C. § 14706); Montreal Convention (Air Freight); CMR Convention (Road)

description: Maximum shipment weight in kilograms at which this contract rate applies. Defines the upper bound of the weight break tier. Null indicates no upper limit (applies to all weights above the minimum). Used in freight cost estimation and audit.
reference: NMFC Weight Break Standards; SAP S/4HANA SD Freight Scales

description: Minimum shipment weight in kilograms at which this contract rate applies. Defines the lower bound of the weight break tier for rate applicability. Used in freight cost estimation and audit to validate correct rate application.
reference: NMFC Weight Break Standards; SAP S/4HANA SD Freight Scales

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the origin country covered by this contract. Used for cross-border freight classification, customs compliance, and international rate applicability.

Geographic origin zone or region covered by this contract for lane-level rate applicability. May represent a state, ZIP zone, city cluster, or carrier-defined zone code. Used in freight cost estimation and tender evaluation.
reference: GS1 GLN; SAP S/4HANA SD Transportation Zones

business_glossary_term: On Time In Full (OTIF) Penalty Rate
description: Contractual penalty rate applied to the carrier for OTIF (On Time In Full) failures, expressed as a percentage of the invoice value or a fixed amount per incident. OTIF is a key KPI in consumer goods supply chain performance management. Supports carrier performance management and deduction processing.
reference: Walmart OTIF Standards; SAP S/4HANA SD Penalty Conditions; CPSC Compliance

business_glossary_term: On Time In Full (OTIF) Threshold Percentage

Internal sustainability performance rating for the facility based on environmental impact, energy efficiency, waste reduction, and sustainable sourcing practices.
IANA time zone identifier for the facility location (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/Berlin) used for production scheduling and shift planning.
Annual water consumption of the facility measured in cubic meters, tracked for environmental compliance and sustainability reporting.
Total number of employees (full-time equivalent) assigned to the manufacturing facility.
Unique identifier for the work center. Primary key.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Labor and overhead budgeting links each work center to a finance cost center for expense tracking.
Reference to the employee responsible for managing and maintaining this work center, supporting accountability and contact management.
Reference to the manufacturing plant where this work center is physically located.
Reference to the production line to which this work center belongs, enabling line-level capacity and performance analysis.
Total available production hours per day for this work center after accounting for planned downtime, breaks, and maintenance windows.
Next scheduled calibration date for measurement and control instruments on this work center, ensuring accuracy and compliance with quality standards.
Unit of measure for the rated capacity indicating how production output is quantified for this work center.

ISO 14644 clean room classification for work centers in controlled environments, critical for cosmetics and personal care product manufacturing per GMP requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: iso_3|iso_4|iso_5|iso_6|iso_7|iso_8|not_applicable — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Date when the work center was first commissioned and put into production service, establishing the asset lifecycle baseline.
Timestamp when this work center record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage.
Standard number of operators required to run this work center during normal production operations, used for labor planning and scheduling.
Date when the work center was retired from production service, supporting asset lifecycle tracking and capacity planning.
Average energy consumption in kilowatt-hours per operating hour, supporting sustainability reporting and cost allocation per ISO 14001 environmental management.

Current qualification status of the work center per GMP requirements. IQ (Installation Qualification), OQ (Operational Qualification), PQ (Performance Qualification) track equipment validation stages per ISO 22716.

Electrical area classification for work centers handling flammable or explosive materials, ensuring compliance with Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) and ATEX directives.
