Indicates whether this work center operates in a humidity-controlled environment requiring environmental monitoring per GMP standards.
Date of the most recent calibration performed on this work center, supporting traceability and compliance documentation.
Classification of the work center by maintenance priority and frequency requirements, driving preventive maintenance scheduling.
Maintenance approach applied to this work center defining how maintenance activities are planned and executed.
Name of the equipment manufacturer, supporting warranty management, spare parts procurement, and technical support.
Unique equipment identifier in the Siemens Opcenter MES system enabling real-time production tracking and shop floor data collection.
Manufacturer model number of the work center equipment, enabling precise identification for maintenance, parts ordering, and technical documentation.
Timestamp when this work center record was last modified, supporting change tracking and audit compliance.
Minimum operator skill level required to operate this work center safely and effectively, supporting workforce planning and training requirements.
Date when the work center achieved its current GMP qualification status, establishing the baseline for requalification scheduling.
Maximum production capacity of the work center expressed in units per time period, used for Material Requirements Planning (MRP) capacity calculations.
Date by which the work center must undergo requalification to maintain GMP compliance and production authorization.
Safety certifications held by this work center such as CE marking, UL listing, or other regulatory approvals required for operation.
reference: OSHA Safety Standards, CE Marking Directive

description: Unique serial number assigned by the manufacturer to this specific equipment unit, supporting warranty tracking and asset identification.
Standard time in minutes required to prepare the work center for production, including changeover and configuration activities.
reference: SAP PP Routing and Work Center

description: Standard shift pattern for this work center defining operational hours and crew rotation schedules.
Standard time in minutes required to complete one production cycle or unit at this work center, used for scheduling and costing.
reference: SAP PP Routing and Work Center

description: Standard time in minutes required to clean, sanitize, and reset the work center after production completion per Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) requirements.
Indicates whether this work center operates in a temperature-controlled environment requiring environmental monitoring per GMP standards.
Target utilization rate as a percentage of available capacity, used for capacity planning and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) benchmarking.
High-level category grouping work centers by operational domain for capacity planning and resource allocation.
Business identifier code for the work center used in production planning and scheduling systems. Externally known unique code.
Detailed description of the work center including its purpose, capabilities, and operational characteristics.
Human-readable name of the work center for identification and reporting purposes.
Current operational status of the work center indicating availability for production scheduling and capacity planning.
Classification of the work center by its primary function in the manufacturing process. Categorizes equipment by operational role.
Unique identifier for the bill of materials record. Primary key for the manufacturing BOM entity.
Reference to the finished good or semi-finished SKU that this BOM defines. Links to the product master for which this material structure applies.
reference: GS1 Global Trade Item Number Standards

description: Reference to the preferred or sole-source supplier for this component. Used for procurement planning, supplier performance tracking, and supply chain risk management. Nullable if multiple suppliers are available.

Indicates whether this component contains or may contain allergens as defined by FDA and EU REACH regulations. True if allergen present. Used for product labeling, consumer safety warnings, and regulatory compliance.
reference: FDA Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act

description: Identifier for a group of interchangeable components that can substitute for each other in production. Used for supply chain flexibility, multi-sourcing strategies, and material availability optimization.

The selection priority for this component within its alternative item group. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used by MRP to determine preferred material selection when multiple alternatives are available.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Alternative BOM Selection

description: The date when this BOM version was formally approved for production use. Establishes the official release date for regulatory compliance and change control purposes.

The name or identifier of the person who approved this BOM version for production use. Required for GMP compliance and quality assurance. Typically a product development manager, quality manager, or regulatory affairs specialist.

Indicates whether this component is automatically consumed (backflushed) when the finished good is confirmed in the MES system, rather than requiring explicit material issue transactions. True if backflushed. Common for high-volume, low-value components.
The reference quantity of the finished good for which the component quantities are defined. Typically 1 unit, 100 units, or 1 batch. All component quantities are expressed per this base quantity.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP BOM Base Quantity

description: The unit of measure for the base quantity (e.g., EA for each, KG for kilogram, L for liter, BOX for box). Must align with the SKU primary UOM.
The externally-known unique business identifier for this BOM, typically assigned by the PLM or ERP system. Used for cross-system reference and production order material requirements.
Current lifecycle status of the BOM. Active BOMs are used for production planning and MRP runs. Inactive or obsolete BOMs are retained for historical reference and regulatory traceability.

Classification of the BOM structure. Production BOM is used for standard manufacturing, co-product for joint production scenarios, phantom for intermediate assemblies not stocked, engineering for R&D prototypes, and planning for demand forecasting.
The date after which this specific component is no longer valid within the BOM structure. Nullable for open-ended components. Used for material phase-out and supplier transition management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP BOM Component Validity

description: The date from which this specific component becomes valid within the BOM structure. Supports phased material transitions, supplier changes, and cost optimization initiatives.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP BOM Component Validity

description: Classification of the component type. Stock items are inventory-managed materials, non-stock are direct procurement items, phantom are intermediate assemblies not physically stocked, text items are instructions, and variable size items have flexible dimensions.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP BOM Item Categories

description: Sequential line number for each component within the BOM structure. Defines the order of components for display, reporting, and regulatory ingredient listing (descending order by weight for INCI compliance).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP BOM Item Number

description: The quantity of this component required to produce the base quantity of the finished good. Used for MRP explosion, production order material requirements, and COGS calculation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP BOM Component Quantity

description: The unit of measure for the component quantity (e.g., KG for raw materials, EA for packaging units, L for liquids). Must align with the component material master UOM.

The percentage of total product cost attributed to this component. Used for COGS calculation, profitability analysis, and cost optimization initiatives. Sum of all component cost allocations should equal 100% for the BOM.
The date and time when this BOM record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and regulatory compliance documentation per ISO 9001 requirements.

Indicates whether this component is critical for product quality, safety, or regulatory compliance. True if critical. Triggers enhanced quality control, supplier qualification requirements, and inventory safety stock policies.
The date after which this BOM version is no longer valid for new production orders. Nullable for open-ended BOMs. Used for phase-out management and regulatory compliance transitions.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP BOM Validity Period

description: The date from which this BOM version becomes valid for production planning and MRP explosion. Supports planned material transitions and new product launches.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP BOM Validity Period

description: Indicates whether this component is classified as a hazardous material requiring special handling, storage, and disposal per OSHA and EPA regulations. True if hazardous. Triggers safety data sheet requirements and GMP compliance protocols.

business_glossary_term: International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients (INCI) Name
description: The standardized INCI name for cosmetic ingredients as required by FDA and EU regulations. Used for product labeling, regulatory submissions, and consumer transparency. Mandatory for personal care and cosmetic products.
The date and time when this BOM record was last updated. Tracks formulation changes, component substitutions, and regulatory updates. Critical for change control and GMP compliance.

The procurement or production lead time for this component in days. Used for MRP scheduling, production order release timing, and inventory planning. Includes supplier lead time plus internal processing time.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP MRP Lead Time Scheduling

description: Defines the lot sizing rule for this component in production orders. Exact requires precise quantity, minimum allows overages, multiple requires quantities in specific increments, none has no restriction. Impacts material planning and waste management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Lot Sizing Procedures

description: The minimum quantity that must be procured or produced for this component. Driven by supplier MOQ, production batch constraints, or economic order quantity calculations. Nullable if no minimum applies.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Minimum Order Quantity

description: External reference identifier linking this BOM to the source PLM system record. Enables traceability to engineering change orders, formulation documents, and R&D specifications.

Free-text field capturing regulatory compliance requirements, restrictions, or special handling instructions for this component. Includes FDA registration numbers, EU REACH compliance status, GMP requirements, and safety data sheet references.
reference: FDA CFR Title 21, EU REACH Regulation

description: The expected waste or loss percentage for this component during production. Used to adjust gross material requirements in MRP runs. Typical values range from 0% to 10% depending on material type and process complexity.

Certification or standard that this component meets for sustainable sourcing (e.g., FSC for paper, RSPO for palm oil, Fair Trade, Organic). Used for corporate sustainability reporting and consumer transparency initiatives.
reference: FSC Chain of Custody, RSPO Certification

description: Version identifier for the BOM structure. Incremented when material composition changes due to reformulation, cost optimization, or regulatory compliance updates. Supports change control and audit trail.
Unique system-generated identifier for the planned order record. Primary key for the planned order entity.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Planned Order Object

description: Reference to the production order that was created from this planned order upon conversion. Null if not yet converted.
Reference to the production planner or planning team responsible for managing this planned order.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Planner Assignment

description: Reference to the manufacturing plant or facility where production is planned to occur.
Reference to the SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) that this planned order is for. Links to the product master data.
Foreign key linking to customer.trade_account. Business justification: Supports demand‑planning reports linking planned production to specific customer accounts and forecast agreements.
Foreign key linking to promotion.trade_promotion. Business justification: Planned Promotional Production aligns MRP planned orders with upcoming trade promotions to ensure supply availability.
The date when the produced or procured material from this planned order is expected to be available for consumption or shipment.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Availability Check

description: The date when this planned order was converted to a production order. Null if not yet converted.
Indicates whether this planned order has been converted to a production order: NOT_CONVERTED (still in planning), PARTIALLY_CONVERTED (split conversion), FULLY_CONVERTED (completely converted).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Order Conversion

description: User ID or system identifier of the person or automated process that created this planned order.
System timestamp when this planned order record was first created in the system.
Reference number or identifier of the originating demand document (sales order number, forecast ID, transfer request number, etc.).

Classification of the demand signal that triggered this planned order: FORECAST (demand planning), CUSTOMER_ORDER (firm sales order), STOCK_TRANSFER (inter-plant), SAFETY_STOCK (replenishment), PROMOTION (trade promotion demand).

business_glossary_term: Material Requirements Planning (MRP) Exception Message Code
description: Code representing MRP exception conditions (e.g., EX01 = reschedule in, EX02 = reschedule out, EX03 = cancel, EX10 = expedite). Empty if no exception.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - MRP Exception Messages

description: Human-readable description of the MRP exception condition requiring planner attention.
The date when this planned order was firmed by a planner. Null if not yet firmed.
Boolean flag indicating whether this planned order is firmed (locked from automatic MRP changes). True = firmed, False = subject to MRP rescheduling.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Firming Logic

description: Indicates whether this planned order must comply with GMP regulations. True for pharmaceutical and cosmetic products requiring ISO 22716 compliance.
reference: ISO 22716 - Good Manufacturing Practices for Cosmetics

description: Version identifier from SAP IBP system that generated the demand signal driving this planned order. Format: IBP-YYYYMM.
User ID or system identifier of the person or automated process that last modified this planned order.
System timestamp when this planned order record was last updated or modified.
Code indicating the lot-sizing procedure used: EX (exact lot size), HB (lot-for-lot), FX (fixed lot size), PD (periodic lot size), WM (weekly lot size).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Lot Sizing

description: Code identifying the MRP controller or planning group responsible for this material and plant combination.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - MRP Controller

description: Reference to the specific MRP run that generated or last modified this planned order. Links to MRP execution history.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - MRP Run

description: Free-text field for planners to add comments, special instructions, or contextual information about this planned order.
Business-readable unique identifier for the planned order, typically system-generated following organizational numbering conventions.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Planned Order Number

description: Current lifecycle status of the planned order: DRAFT (initial creation), FIRMED (locked from MRP changes), RELEASED (approved for execution), CONVERTED (converted to production order), DELETED (marked for deletion), CANCELLED (cancelled before conversion).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Order Status

description: Classification of the planned order origin: MPS (Master Production Schedule), MRP (Material Requirements Planning generated), CBP (Consumption-Based Planning), MANUAL (manually created), FORECAST (forecast-driven), SAFETY (safety stock replenishment).
The quantity of the SKU planned to be produced or procured in this order, expressed in the base unit of measure.
The planning time bucket this order belongs to, expressed as YYYY-Wnn (week), YYYY-Mnn (month), or YYYY-Qn (quarter). Used for MPS and S&OP alignment.
Two-digit code defining the planning strategy (e.g., 10 = make-to-stock, 20 = make-to-order, 40 = planning with final assembly, 50 = planning without final assembly).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Planning Strategies

description: Priority level assigned to this planned order for scheduling and resource allocation: LOW, NORMAL, HIGH, URGENT.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Priority Management

description: Indicates whether this planned order is for in-house production (IN_HOUSE), external procurement (EXTERNAL), or can be either (BOTH).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Procurement Type

description: Identifies the specific combination of BOM (Bill of Materials) and routing to be used for production. Links to production master data.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Production Version

description: The inventory level that triggers generation of a planned order for replenishment.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Reorder Point Planning

description: The safety stock level maintained for this SKU at this plant, influencing planned order generation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Safety Stock

description: Version identifier for the MPS schedule that generated or governs this planned order. Enables tracking of schedule changes over time.
The planned date when production or procurement activities for this order should be completed and goods available.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Basic Dates

description: The planned date when production or procurement activities for this order should begin.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Basic Dates

business_glossary_term: Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) Cycle Reference
description: Reference to the S&OP planning cycle that this planned order aligns with. Format: SOP-YYYY-Mnn or SOP-YYYY-Qn.
The unit of measure for the planned quantity (e.g., EA for each, KG for kilogram, L for liter). Follows ISO standard unit codes.
Unique identifier for the production order. Primary key for the production order entity.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Production Order Master

description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Cost accounting report requires each production order to be charged to a finance cost center for OPEX allocation.

Foreign key linking to quality.inspection_plan. Business justification: Production orders trigger an inspection plan; linking allows the order execution system to retrieve the exact inspection plan governing sampling and testing for that batch.

Foreign key linking to manufacturing.manufacturing_bom. Business justification: Production order consumes a specific manufacturing BOM; adding manufacturing_bom_id FK connects BOM to order and eliminates isolation of manufacturing_bom.
Foreign key linking to marketing.brand. Business justification: Production Planning Dashboard ties orders to brands to enable demand forecasting and coordinated marketing launch planning.
Reference to the bill of materials used for this production order. Defines component requirements.
FK to manufacturing.production_line

Foreign key linking to research.rd_project. Business justification: Pilot production orders are generated from R&D projects; the Production Planning system needs the project ID to track development cost and schedule.

Foreign key linking to regulatory.registration. Business justification: Production order compliance reporting requires linking each order to the product's registration record to verify GMP compliance and traceability.
Foreign key linking to manufacturing.routing. Business justification: Each production order follows a routing; adding routing_id FK links routing to order and eliminates isolation of routing.

Foreign key linking to sales.order. Business justification: Order fulfillment process requires linking each production order to the originating sales order to track manufacturing against sales commitments.
Reference to the SKU being produced in this production order. Links to the product master data.
reference: GS1 Global Trade Item Number Standards

description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Order‑level supervisor oversees execution, cost tracking and GMP compliance; required for order‑performance dashboards.
Foreign key linking to customer.trade_account. Business justification: Required for Production Order to Customer Account linkage for OTIF SLA reporting and order fulfillment traceability.
Actual cost incurred for the production order. Includes material, labor, and overhead costs. Used for variance analysis.
Actual date and time when production execution completed. Used for OEE calculation and performance analysis.
Actual date and time when production execution began on the shop floor. Captured from MES system.
Unique batch or lot number assigned to the production run. Critical for traceability and recall management per GMP requirements.
Time in minutes required for line changeover before starting this production order. Used for scheduling and efficiency analysis.
Actual quantity produced and confirmed as good output. Represents yield after quality inspection.
Cost object (production order number or process order) used for collecting actual costs. Links to CO-PC product costing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Product Cost Controlling

description: Date and time when the production order was created in the system. First event in order lifecycle.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for cost amounts. Typically company code currency.
Total unplanned downtime in minutes during production execution. Impacts OEE availability component.
Indicates whether this production order is subject to GMP compliance requirements per ISO 22716 standards. True for regulated products.
Inspection lot number created for quality control of the production output. Links to QM inspection results.
Date and time of the most recent update to the production order record. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.
SAP material number for the finished good being produced. Business identifier for the product in ERP system.
Three-character code identifying the MRP controller responsible for planning this material. Links to planner master data.
Free-text notes or comments related to the production order. Captures special instructions, issues, or observations from shop floor.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Order Header Text

description: Overall Equipment Effectiveness percentage for this production run. Calculated as Availability × Performance × Quality. Industry standard KPI.
Business identifier for the production order. Externally-known unique order number assigned by SAP S/4HANA PP system.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Production Order Master

description: Planned quantity to be produced in base unit of measure. Target output for the production order.

Current lifecycle status of the production order. CRTD=Created, REL=Released, PCNF=Partially Confirmed, TECO=Technically Complete, CNF=Confirmed, DLV=Delivered, CLSD=Closed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CRTD|REL|PCNF|TECO|CNF|DLV|CLSD — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Order Status System

description: Classification of production order. PP01=Standard Production, PP03=Rework, PP05=Co-Product, PP10=Process Order, PP20=Batch Order.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Order Type Configuration

description: Standard or planned cost for producing the order quantity. Calculated from BOM and routing costs.
Four-character code identifying the manufacturing facility where production occurs. Maps to SAP plant master.
Priority level for production scheduling. 1=Highest priority (rush/expedite), 5=Lowest priority (standard). Used for sequencing and resource allocation.
Name of the production supervisor responsible for overseeing execution of this order on the shop floor.
Production version defining the specific BOM and routing combination used. Enables multiple production methods for same material.
Indicates whether quality inspection is mandatory before goods receipt. Drives QM integration and inspection lot creation.
User ID of the person who released the production order for execution. Audit trail for production authorization.
Date and time when the production order was released for shop floor execution. Triggers material availability check and capacity reservation.
Routing or recipe number defining the sequence of operations for production. Links to work center and operation master data.
Planned date when production is scheduled to complete. Used for capacity planning and delivery commitments.
Planned date when production is scheduled to begin. Set during production planning and MRP run.
Quantity of material scrapped or rejected during production. Used for yield analysis and cost accounting.
Rule for settling production order costs. FUL=Full settlement, PAR=Partial settlement, PER=Periodic settlement.
Base unit of measure for quantities. Standard ISO codes such as EA (each), KG (kilogram), L (liter), M (meter).
Actual yield percentage calculated as (confirmed_quantity / order_quantity) * 100. Key performance metric for production efficiency.
User ID of the person who created the production order in the system. Audit trail for order origination.
Unique identifier for the production routing master record. Primary key.
Reference to the Bill of Materials (BOM) that defines the raw materials and components consumed by this routing. Links routing to material requirements.
User identifier of the person who created this routing record. Supports audit trail and data lineage.
User identifier of the person who approved this routing for production use. Supports audit trail and compliance requirements.
User identifier of the person who last modified this routing record. Supports audit trail and change tracking.
Reference to the finished or semi-finished SKU that this routing defines the manufacturing process for.
Approval status of the routing for production use. Approved routings are validated and authorized; pending routings await review; rejected routings require rework.
Date and time when this routing was approved for production use. Supports audit trail and compliance requirements.
Standard production lot size for which the routing operation times and resource requirements are defined. Used as the basis for scaling production schedules.
Unit of measure for the base quantity (e.g., KG, L, EA, M). Aligns with GS1 unit codes.
Time required to transition production lines from the previous product to this routing. Critical for production scheduling and minimizing downtime.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the standard cost amount.
Date and time when this routing record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.
Overall expected scrap percentage for the routing, representing anticipated waste or defects. Used for material planning and cost estimation.
Overall expected yield percentage for the routing, representing the ratio of good output to total input. Used for production planning and variance analysis.
Indicates whether this routing includes GMP-critical operations requiring enhanced documentation, validation, and compliance controls per ISO 22716 and FDA regulations.
Number of in-process control checkpoints defined in this routing. IPC checkpoints are quality inspection points during production per ISO 22716 and GMP requirements.
Date and time when this routing record was last modified. Supports audit trail and change tracking.

Constraint on production lot sizes for this routing. Fixed requires exact base quantity; minimum/maximum define bounds; multiple requires lot sizes to be multiples of base quantity; none allows any lot size.
Maximum production lot size allowed for this routing. Nullable if no maximum constraint exists.
Minimum production lot size allowed for this routing. Nullable if no minimum constraint exists.

JSON array or delimited string capturing the complete sequence of operation steps. Each operation includes: operation_number, work_center_code, operation_description, control_key (internal_processing|external_processing|milestone), setup_time_minutes, machine_time_minutes, labor_time_minutes, yield_quantity, scrap_percentage, gmp_critical_step_flag, ipc_checkpoint_flag. This is the single authoritative source for all routing operation data — no separate operation entity exists.
Manufacturing plant or facility where this routing is executed. Aligns with organizational plant master data.
Code identifying the production scheduling strategy or algorithm used for this routing (e.g., forward scheduling, backward scheduling, finite capacity).
Detailed textual description of the routing, including its purpose, scope, and any special instructions for production planners and shop floor operators.
Business identifier for the routing. Externally-known unique code used in production planning and scheduling systems.

Current lifecycle status of the routing. Active routings are available for production scheduling; draft routings are under development; inactive routings are temporarily disabled; obsolete routings are retired; under_review routings are pending approval.

Classification of the routing defining its usage pattern. Standard routings are default production paths; reference routings are templates; rate routings define production rates; alternative routings provide backup paths; special routings are for one-time or custom production runs.
Standard production cost per base quantity for this routing, including labor, machine, and overhead costs. Used for cost accounting and variance analysis.
Cumulative labor time across all operations in the routing, used for workforce planning and standard cost calculation.
Cumulative machine processing time across all operations in the routing, used for capacity planning and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) calculations.
Cumulative setup time across all operations in the routing, used for capacity planning and scheduling.

Total cumulative lead time in hours required to complete all operations in this routing, including setup, processing, and queue times. Used for Material Requirements Planning (MRP) and capacity planning.
Date from which this routing becomes effective and available for production scheduling.
Date until which this routing remains effective. Nullable for open-ended routings.
Version identifier for the routing, enabling tracking of routing changes over time. Supports engineering change management and audit trails.
Unique identifier for the electronic batch manufacturing record (eBMR). Primary key for GMP-compliant batch traceability.

Foreign key linking to sustainability.carbon_offset. Business justification: Batch‑level carbon neutrality uses purchased offsets; linking batch to offset record provides traceability and reporting of offset usage.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Batch cost roll‑up uses finance cost center to allocate raw material and labor expenses per batch.
Foreign key linking to inventory.lot_batch. Business justification: Regulatory traceability: links each production batch to its inventory lot batch for recall investigations and quality audits.
Foreign key linking to manufacturing.manufacturing_facility. Business justification: Batch record should reference the specific manufacturing facility for traceability.
Foreign key linking to marketing.brand. Business justification: Brand Batch Traceability Report requires linking each batch to its brand for recall, quality and marketing performance analysis.
Reference to the quality assurance personnel who performed final batch release. Links to workforce master data.
Reference to the specific production line used for this batch. Links to equipment master data.
Reference to the production order that authorized this batch manufacturing run. Links to SAP PP production order master.

Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Batch‑to‑PO traceability is needed for audit, recall, and cost allocation linking each manufactured batch to its sourcing PO.

Foreign key linking to research.research_formulation. Business justification: Traceability report requires linking each manufacturing batch to the exact formulation used, essential for regulatory compliance and product recall.
Foreign key linking to sales.order. Business justification: Batch traceability for recalls and quality investigations needs to associate each batch with the sales order that generated the demand.
Reference to the finished goods SKU produced in this batch. Links to product master data.
Actual cost per unit incurred for this batch. Includes material, labor, and overhead variances.
Unique manufacturing batch identifier assigned at production initiation. Used for product traceability and recall management per GMP requirements.
Actual production quantity achieved for this batch. Used for yield calculation and inventory reconciliation.
Planned production quantity for this batch as specified in the production order. Measured in base unit of measure.
Current lifecycle status of the batch. Controls inventory availability and distribution eligibility per GMP workflow.
Version of the bill of materials used for this batch. Ensures traceability of raw material specifications.
Time in minutes required for line changeover before this batch. Key metric for SMED and lean manufacturing initiatives.
Date and time when this batch record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record lifecycle.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for cost amounts. Supports multi-currency manufacturing operations.
Total unplanned downtime in minutes during batch production. Used for OEE calculation and maintenance planning.
Number of electronic signatures captured during batch record lifecycle. Required for FDA 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.
Date after which the product should not be used or sold. Critical for FEFO inventory management and consumer safety.
Number of GMP deviations recorded for this batch. Used for quality trend analysis and CAPA tracking.
Indicates whether any GMP deviations were recorded during batch production. Triggers quality review workflow.
Date and time when this batch record was last updated. Audit trail for GMP compliance and data integrity.
Indicates whether complete raw material lot traceability has been captured for this batch. Required for recall readiness.
Calendar date of batch production. Printed on product packaging for consumer information and regulatory compliance.
Date and time when batch production was completed and final packaging finished. Used for cycle time analysis.
Date and time when batch production was initiated on the shop floor. Captured from MES system.
Overall equipment effectiveness achieved during batch production. Composite metric of availability, performance, and quality.
Indicates whether the batch has been released by Quality Assurance for distribution. Required before inventory availability.
Date and time when Quality Assurance approved the batch for release. Marks transition from quarantine to available inventory.
Indicates whether this batch is subject to a product recall. Triggers supply chain hold and customer notification.
Date when recall was initiated for this batch. Used for regulatory reporting and recall effectiveness tracking.
Indicates whether this batch record is locked from further edits. Required for GMP record integrity after quality release.
Indicates whether batch is on regulatory hold pending investigation or approval. Prevents distribution until cleared.
Quantity of product requiring rework during batch production. Indicator of process capability and quality issues.
Version of the production routing used for this batch. Documents the manufacturing process steps executed.
Quantity of product scrapped during batch production. Used for yield calculation and waste reduction analysis.
Number of days between manufacturing date and expiry date. Derived from product stability testing.
Standard cost per unit for this batch based on BOM and routing. Used for cost variance analysis.
Unit of measure for batch size quantities (e.g., KG, LTR, EA, CS). Aligns with GS1 standards.
Reference to the master batch record document stored in Veeva Vault. Links to regulatory document management system.
Ratio of actual batch size to planned batch size expressed as percentage. Key performance indicator for manufacturing efficiency.
Unique identifier for the changeover event. Primary key for the changeover record.
Identifier of the primary operator or technician responsible for executing the changeover.
Identifier of the quality assurance inspector who verified and approved the changeover completion and cleaning procedures.
Identifier of the SKU that was being produced before the changeover.
Foreign key linking to manufacturing.manufacturing_facility. Business justification: Changeover events occur at a specific manufacturing facility; link directly to manufacturing_facility.
Identifier of the production line or work center where the changeover was executed.
Identifier of the production order that triggered or required this changeover event.
Identifier of the SKU that will be produced after the changeover.
FK to manufacturing.work_center
Actual elapsed time in minutes from changeover start to completion, calculated from actual start and end timestamps.
Actual date and time when the changeover execution was completed and the line was ready for production.
Actual date and time when the changeover execution began on the shop floor.
Current lifecycle status of the changeover event indicating its progress through the execution workflow.

Classification of the changeover based on the nature of the change: flavor (product variant), format (packaging type), size (package size), cleaning (sanitation), material (raw material switch), or color (product color change).
Date and time when the GMP cleaning verification was completed and approved by quality assurance.
Date and time when this changeover record was first created in the system.
Standardized code indicating the primary reason for any delays or extended downtime during the changeover.
Detailed description of the reason for any delays or extended downtime during the changeover execution.
Indicates whether mechanical or equipment adjustments were required as part of the changeover process.
Percentage of production output that met quality standards on the first production run immediately following the changeover, indicating changeover quality effectiveness.

business_glossary_term: Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Cleaning Verified Flag
description: Indicates whether the required GMP cleaning and sanitation procedures were completed and verified as part of the changeover process.
Identifier linking this changeover to a specific continuous improvement initiative or project.
Quantity of raw material or work-in-process material wasted or scrapped during the changeover, measured in kilograms.
Free-text notes or comments from operators, supervisors, or quality inspectors regarding the changeover execution, issues encountered, or lessons learned.
Calculated impact of this changeover event on the production lines overall equipment effectiveness for the shift or day, expressed as a percentage.
Planned date and time when the changeover was scheduled to be completed according to the production schedule.
Planned date and time when the changeover was scheduled to begin according to the production schedule.
Code identifying the production shift during which the changeover occurred.

business_glossary_term: Single-Minute Exchange of Die (SMED) Improvement Flag
description: Indicates whether this changeover was part of a SMED continuous improvement initiative or pilot program.
Standard or target duration in minutes for this type of changeover based on engineering standards and historical performance.
Number of operators or technicians involved in executing the changeover.
Indicates whether tooling or die changes were required as part of the changeover process.
Date and time when this changeover record was last modified or updated in the system.
Difference in minutes between actual and standard changeover duration. Positive values indicate the changeover took longer than standard; negative values indicate faster than standard performance.
Unique identifier for the downtime event record. Primary key for the downtime event entity.

Identifier of the production operator who reported or was present during the downtime event.
Identifier of the production line where the downtime event occurred.
Identifier of the production order that was impacted by this downtime event.
Identifier of the production shift during which the downtime event occurred.

Indicates whether production batches affected by this downtime event require quality hold pending investigation.
Description of the corrective action taken to resolve the downtime event and restore production.
Timestamp when this downtime event record was first created in the data platform.
Three-letter ISO currency code for the financial impact amount.
Source system or method by which the downtime event was captured (MES automatic detection, manual operator entry, sensor, SCADA).

Timestamp when the downtime event ended and production resumed. Null if downtime is ongoing.
Timestamp when the downtime event began. Captured from MES system or manual entry.
Indicates whether the downtime was planned (scheduled maintenance, changeover) or unplanned (breakdown, shortage).
Total duration of the downtime event measured in minutes. Calculated as the difference between end and start timestamps.

Level of management escalation required or triggered by this downtime event based on duration and impact.

Indicates whether this downtime event is included in OEE availability loss calculations.

Current status of the downtime event resolution process.

Unique surrogate identifier for the GMP compliance event record. Primary key for the gmp_event data product. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — represents a discrete GMP compliance business event with a clear lifecycle.

Reference to the quality manager or authorized person who reviewed and electronically signed off on the GMP event record. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature compliance. Nullable until event reaches approval stage.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 22716 Section 10; Veeva Vault Electronic Signature

description: Reference to the manufacturing batch record against which this GMP event was detected. Links the compliance event to the specific production batch in the batch record master. Serves as the PARTY_REFERENCE (resource reference) category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.

Reference to the Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) record initiated in response to this GMP event. Nullable when no CAPA has been raised yet or when event severity does not require CAPA. Managed in Veeva Vault Quality module.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; Veeva Vault CAPA Module

description: Reference to the specific piece of manufacturing equipment involved in or associated with the GMP event. Particularly relevant for equipment_failure and process_parameter_breach event types. Links to equipment master in SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) module.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PM Module; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68; ISO 22716 Section 6

description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.manufacturing_facility. Business justification: GMP events must be linked to the specific manufacturing facility where they occurred.

Reference to the employee (operator, quality technician, or supervisor) who first detected and reported the GMP event. Links to Workday HCM employee master. Required for GMP accountability and electronic signature audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 22716 Section 10; Workday HCM

description: Reference to the previous GMP event of the same type that this event is a recurrence of. Populated only when recurrence_flag is true. Enables recurrence trend analysis and CAPA effectiveness assessment across event lineage.
FK to manufacturing.production_line

Reference to the SAP S/4HANA PP production order or Siemens Opcenter MES work order associated with this GMP event. Enables traceability from compliance event back to the manufacturing execution context.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module; Siemens Opcenter MES; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.100

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.registration. Business justification: GMP event investigations reference the product registration to ensure corrective actions align with the approved registration details.
Reference to the SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) being manufactured when the GMP event occurred. Enables product-level compliance traceability, recall risk assessment, and regulatory reporting by product.
reference: GS1 Standards; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.130; ISO 22716

description: Foreign key linking to procurement.supplier. Business justification: Regulatory GMP incident reports must identify the raw‑material supplier causing the event for root‑cause analysis.

Quantity of product (in the batch unit of measure) potentially affected by the GMP event. Used for impact assessment, recall scope estimation, and financial exposure calculation. Serves as the QUANTITATIVE_RESULT measurement for this non-monetary transaction.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 8; SAP S/4HANA QM

description: Unit of measure for the affected batch quantity (e.g., KG for kilograms, L for liters, EA for each/units). Aligned with GS1 unit of measure codes and SAP S/4HANA base unit of measure configuration.
reference: GS1 Unit of Measure Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM; ISO 22716

description: Date and time when the authorized quality manager electronically signed and approved the GMP event record. Distinct from detection and creation timestamps. Required for regulatory audit trail and SLA compliance measurement.

Quality disposition decision for the affected batch resulting from the GMP event investigation. released: batch meets quality standards and is approved for distribution. quarantined: batch held pending investigation outcome. rejected: batch fails quality standards and cannot be released. reworked: batch underwent approved rework procedure. destroyed: batch disposed of due to quality failure.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.165; ISO 22716 Section 9; SAP S/4HANA QM Batch Disposition

description: Human-readable batch or lot number of the product being manufactured when the GMP event was detected. Denormalized from the batch record for direct traceability in compliance reports and regulatory submissions without requiring a join.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.130; ISO 22716 Section 8; GS1 SSCC Standards

description: Identifier of the Critical Control Point (CCP) in the manufacturing process where the GMP event was detected. Applicable for process_parameter_breach and environmental_monitoring_excursion event types. Aligned with HACCP and GMP process control frameworks.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.110; ISO 22716 Section 7; HACCP Codex Alimentarius

description: Date and time when the GMP event was formally closed after all required CAPA actions were completed and verified effective. Nullable for open or in-progress events. Used to calculate event resolution cycle time for quality KPI reporting.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; ICH Q10

description: Date and time when the immediate containment action was executed following GMP event detection (e.g., line stoppage, batch quarantine). Used to calculate detection-to-containment response time, a key GMP performance metric.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; ICH Q10

description: Timestamp when the GMP event record was first created in the system (Veeva Vault or SAP QM). Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68 (Electronic Records); 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 22716

description: Date and time when the GMP compliance event was first detected or observed on the shop floor or in the laboratory. This is the principal real-world event time (BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category). Distinct from the record creation timestamp. Critical for regulatory timelines and investigation SLA tracking.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; Siemens Opcenter MES

description: Electronic signature token or hash of the approver who reviewed and closed the GMP event record, as required by FDA 21 CFR Part 11. Captures the meaning of the signature (e.g., 'Reviewed and Approved'), the signer identity reference, and timestamp encoded in the token. Managed by Veeva Vault e-signature module.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 22716 Section 10; Veeva Vault Electronic Signature

description: ISO cleanroom classification zone or EU GMP environmental grade where the GMP event occurred. Relevant for environmental_monitoring_excursion event types. Grade A/B are highest cleanliness requirements; Grade C/D are controlled areas. Used for contamination risk assessment.
reference: EU GMP Annex 1; ISO 14644 Cleanroom Standards; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.42

description: Detailed narrative description of the GMP compliance event, including what was observed, where it occurred, and the immediate circumstances. Captured by the detecting operator or quality technician at time of detection. Serves as the QUANTITATIVE_RESULT (qualitative payload) category for non-monetary TRANSACTION_HEADER.

Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the GMP compliance event, used in regulatory submissions, CAPA tracking, and cross-system references. Format: GMP-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: ISO 22716; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; Veeva Vault Quality Document Numbering

description: Risk-based severity classification of the GMP event. Critical: potential impact on product safety or patient/consumer harm; requires immediate escalation and regulatory notification. Major: significant departure from GMP requirements with potential quality impact. Minor: low-risk deviation with minimal quality impact. Drives CAPA prioritization and regulatory reporting obligations.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management

description: Current lifecycle status of the GMP compliance event. open: newly detected, investigation not yet started. under_investigation: root cause analysis in progress. pending_capa: investigation complete, awaiting CAPA closure. closed: all actions completed and verified effective. cancelled: event determined to be erroneous or duplicate. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; Veeva Vault Quality Workflow

description: Classification of the GMP compliance event by its nature. Values: deviation (unplanned departure from approved procedure), oos_result (Out-of-Specification laboratory result), environmental_monitoring_excursion (EM limit breach), equipment_failure (critical equipment malfunction), process_parameter_breach (critical process parameter out of range), contamination_event (microbial or cross-contamination incident). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: deviation|oos_result|environmental_monitoring_excursion|equipment_failure|process_parameter_breach|contamination_event — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; ICH Q10

description: Description of the immediate containment or corrective action taken at the time of GMP event detection to prevent further impact (e.g., line stoppage, batch quarantine, equipment isolation). Distinct from the formal CAPA which addresses root cause prevention.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; GMP Good Practice Guidelines

description: Target date by which the root cause investigation must be completed, based on event severity and regulatory SLA requirements. Critical events typically require investigation within 3 business days; major within 10 days; minor within 30 days. Used for overdue investigation tracking.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; ICH Q10

description: Indicates whether this GMP event has been assessed as a potential trigger for a product recall or market withdrawal. True when the event involves a safety risk to consumers that may require removal of product from distribution channels. Activates recall management workflow.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 7 (Recall Policy); CPSC Section 15(b); ISO 22716 Section 10

description: Name or code of the specific manufacturing process step (e.g., mixing, filling, packaging, sterilization, labeling) during which the GMP event was detected. Sourced from Siemens Opcenter MES routing. Used for process-level failure mode analysis.
reference: Siemens Opcenter MES; ISO 22716 Section 7; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.100

description: Indicates whether this GMP event is a recurrence of a previously closed event of the same type at the same facility or production line. True when a similar event has occurred within the past 12 months. Triggers escalated investigation and CAPA effectiveness review.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; ICH Q10

description: Specific regulatory standard or clause that this GMP event relates to or potentially violates. Examples: 'ISO 22716:2007 Section 10.2', 'FDA 21 CFR Part 211.113', 'EU GMP Annex 1'. Used for regulatory submission mapping and compliance gap analysis.
reference: ISO 22716; FDA 21 CFR Part 211; EU GMP Guidelines; CPSC Regulations

description: Date on which the regulatory authority was formally notified of this GMP event. Populated only when regulatory_notification_required is true and notification has been submitted. Used for regulatory compliance timeline tracking.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EU GMP Directive; CPSC Section 15(b) Reporting

description: Indicates whether this GMP event requires formal notification to a regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EU Competent Authority, CPSC). Typically true for critical events involving potential consumer safety risk, product recall triggers, or serious GMP failures. Drives regulatory affairs workflow.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 314.81; EU GMP Directive 2003/94/EC; CPSC Reporting Requirements

description: Quantitative risk score assigned to the GMP event based on ICH Q9 risk assessment methodology, combining probability of occurrence, severity of impact, and detectability. Typically scored on a 1-100 scale. Used for risk-based prioritization of investigations and CAPA resources.
reference: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; ISO 22716 Section 10; FDA Guidance on Quality Risk Management

description: Categorized root cause of the GMP event as determined through investigation. Populated after investigation is complete. Used for trend analysis, systemic failure identification, and CAPA effectiveness measurement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: human_error|equipment_malfunction|raw_material|process_design|environmental|documentation|training — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System

description: Detailed narrative of the identified root cause of the GMP event, as documented by the quality investigator. Populated upon completion of root cause analysis (RCA). Supports regulatory inspection readiness and CAPA justification.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 22716 Section 10; ICH Q10

description: SAP S/4HANA Quality Management (QM) notification number associated with this GMP event. Quality notifications in SAP QM are the operational system of record for defect tracking and corrective actions. Enables reconciliation between the lakehouse and SAP QM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA QM Module; ISO 9001:2015 Section 10.2

description: Manufacturing shift during which the GMP event was detected (e.g., A-shift, B-shift, night shift). Used for shift-level quality performance analysis, operator accountability, and identifying shift-specific patterns in GMP deviations.
reference: Siemens Opcenter MES; SAP S/4HANA PP Shift Management; ISO 22716 Section 5

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the GMP event record. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records regulations.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 22716; Veeva Vault Audit Trail

description: Cross-reference identifier of the corresponding GMP event record in Veeva Vault Quality Document Management system. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the system of record for regulatory document management.
reference: Veeva Vault Quality Module; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 22716

description: Unique identifier for the OEE measurement record. Primary key for the OEE record entity.
Foreign key linking to manufacturing.manufacturing_facility. Business justification: OEE records are captured per manufacturing facility; add direct FK for accurate reporting.
Identifier of the supervisor responsible for the production shift.
Identifier of the specific production line for which OEE was measured.
Identifier of the manufacturing work order executed during this shift.
Identifier of the SKU that was produced during this shift. Links OEE performance to specific product.
Average actual time in seconds to produce one unit during the shift, calculated as Actual Operating Time / Total Units Produced.
Actual time the production line was operating during the shift in minutes, after subtracting unplanned downtime.
Percentage of planned production time that the line was actually operating, calculated as (Planned Production Time - Downtime) / Planned Production Time. Component of OEE calculation.
Manufacturing batch or lot number produced during the shift. Critical for traceability and GMP compliance.
Number of product or format changeovers performed during the shift. Impacts availability and performance metrics.
Total time spent on changeovers during the shift in minutes.
Free-text comments or notes regarding the OEE measurement, including explanations for anomalies or performance issues.
Method by which OEE data was captured (automated from sensors, manual entry, or semi-automated).
Total unplanned downtime during the shift in minutes, including equipment failures, material shortages, and unscheduled stoppages.
Count of units that passed quality inspection and met specifications, calculated as Total Units Produced - Total Units Rejected.
Theoretical minimum time in seconds to produce one unit at maximum design speed under optimal conditions.
Source system identifier for the OEE data, typically Siemens Opcenter MES or equivalent system.
Number of brief stoppages (typically under 5 minutes) that impact performance but may not be classified as downtime.
Composite OEE metric calculated as Availability Rate × Performance Rate × Quality Rate. Single measure of manufacturing productivity and effectiveness.
Current lifecycle status of the OEE record indicating validation and approval state.
Number of operators assigned to the production line during the shift.
Percentage of ideal production speed achieved, calculated as (Ideal Cycle Time × Total Units Produced) / Actual Operating Time. Component of OEE calculation.
Total scheduled production time for the shift in minutes, excluding planned downtime such as breaks and scheduled maintenance.
Time equivalent of production lost due to quality defects and rework in minutes.
Percentage of good units produced without defects, calculated as (Total Units Produced - Total Units Rejected) / Total Units Produced. Component of OEE calculation.
Date and time when the OEE record was first created in the system.
Date and time when the OEE record was last modified.
Count of units that required rework or reprocessing to meet quality standards during the shift.
Total weight of scrap material generated during the shift in kilograms.
Calendar date on which the production shift occurred. Principal business event timestamp for OEE measurement.
Descriptive name of the production shift (e.g., day, evening, night).
Sequential shift identifier within the shift date (e.g., 1 for first shift, 2 for second shift, 3 for third shift).
Time lost due to production running below ideal cycle time in minutes, representing performance inefficiency.
Total count of units produced during the shift, including both good units and rejected units.
Total count of units rejected due to quality defects during the shift.
Number of unplanned production stoppages during the shift.
Date and time when the OEE record was validated by production management.
Unique identifier for the process parameter record. Primary key for in-process control and critical process parameter measurements.
Reference to the batch manufacturing record under which this parameter was measured. Links to the batch master record for traceability.
Reference to the corrective and preventive action (CAPA) record initiated in response to an out-of-specification measurement.
Identifier of the production operator or technician who recorded or verified the parameter measurement. Links to workforce management system.
Identifier of the specific manufacturing equipment or instrument used to measure or control the parameter.
Reference to the product specification or process specification document that defines the control limits for this parameter.
The actual measured value of the process parameter recorded during manufacturing operations.
The date when the measuring instrument or sensor is next due for calibration. Ensures measurement validity per GMP requirements.
Free-text comments or notes recorded by the operator or quality personnel regarding the parameter measurement, including any anomalies or observations.
Boolean indicator whether the measurement result requires corrective action or investigation (True = action required, False = no action needed).
The source system from which the parameter measurement was captured: MES (Manufacturing Execution System), SCADA, LIMS, manual entry, or ERP.
Calculated percentage deviation of the actual value from the target value. Used for trend analysis and process capability assessment.
Code identifying the manufacturing facility or plant where the parameter measurement was recorded. Supports multi-site manufacturing operations.
The lower acceptable boundary for the parameter value. Values below this threshold trigger out-of-specification alerts.
The method used to capture the parameter measurement: manual entry by operator, automated sensor reading, inline PAT sensor, or laboratory analysis.
The date and time when the parameter measurement was taken during the manufacturing process. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Boolean indicator whether the measured value falls outside the defined control limits (True = out of specification, False = within specification).
Name of the process parameter being measured (e.g., temperature, pH, viscosity, fill weight, torque, pressure, mixing speed, dwell time).
Classification of the parameter: CPP (Critical Process Parameter), CQA (Critical Quality Attribute), IPC (In-Process Control), PAT (Process Analytical Technology).
The manufacturing process stage or operation step during which the parameter was measured (e.g., mixing, heating, filling, cooling, packaging).
Identifier of the specific production line within the work center where the parameter was measured. Enables line-level performance analysis.
The date and time when this process parameter record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
The date and time when this process parameter record was last modified. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Boolean indicator whether this parameter measurement must be included in regulatory submissions or audit documentation (True = reportable, False = internal only).
Identifier of the physical sample taken for measurement, if applicable. Links to laboratory information management system (LIMS).
Identifier of the specific sensor or probe that captured the measurement, if applicable. Used for sensor calibration tracking.
Code identifying the production shift during which the parameter measurement was taken (e.g., A, B, C, or day/night shift codes).
The target or setpoint value for the process parameter as defined in the batch master recipe or process specification.
The unit in which the parameter is measured (e.g., Celsius, pH units, cP for viscosity, grams, PSI, RPM, seconds).
The upper acceptable boundary for the parameter value. Values above this threshold trigger out-of-specification alerts.
Status of the parameter measurement verification by quality assurance: pending review, verified as acceptable, rejected, or under investigation.
The date and time when the parameter measurement was verified by quality assurance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Identifier of the quality assurance personnel who verified or approved the parameter measurement record.
Code identifying the manufacturing work center or production line where the parameter was measured. Aligns with SAP PP work center master data.
Unique identifier for the production confirmation record. Primary key for shop floor execution tracking.
Reference to the cost center to which labor and overhead costs for this operation are allocated for financial accounting.
Reference to the manufacturing plant or facility where this operation was performed.
Reference to the shop floor operator or employee who executed and confirmed this manufacturing operation.
Reference to the parent production order under which this operation was executed.
Foreign key linking to sales.order. Business justification: Production confirmation reports must reference the sales order they fulfill for accurate shipping and invoicing.
Reference to the finished or semi-finished material (SKU) produced by this operation.
Reference to the work center (production line, machine, or station) where this operation was performed.
SAP CO activity type code representing the type of work performed (e.g., machine hours, labor hours, setup hours) for cost allocation purposes.
Actual date and time when the operation was completed and confirmed by the operator. Used for OEE calculation and production order settlement.
Actual operator labor time spent on this operation including manual work, monitoring, and quality checks. Measured in minutes.
Actual time the machine or equipment was actively running during this operation. Excludes setup and downtime. Measured in minutes.
Actual time spent on machine setup, changeover, and preparation activities before production began. Measured in minutes.
Actual date and time when the operator began executing this operation on the shop floor. Captured from MES or manual confirmation.
Manufacturing batch or lot number assigned to the output produced in this operation. Critical for traceability and recall management.
Free-text notes or comments entered by the operator or supervisor regarding this operation execution, including any issues or observations.
System timestamp when this confirmation record was created and submitted to the ERP or MES system.
Classification of the confirmation event indicating whether this is a partial progress update, final completion, milestone checkpoint, rework confirmation, or cancellation.
Actual quantity of defective or waste material generated during this operation. Used for yield variance analysis and quality tracking.
Actual quantity of good output produced and confirmed for this operation. Measured in the base unit of measure for the material.
Total unplanned downtime during this operation due to equipment failure, material shortage, or other interruptions. Measured in minutes.
Indicates whether this operation was executed in compliance with GMP standards as required for regulated consumer goods products.
System timestamp when this confirmation record was last updated or modified. Used for change tracking and audit purposes.
Unique transaction reference from the Siemens Opcenter MES system that originated this confirmation. Used for traceability and system reconciliation.
Calculated availability component of OEE for this operation, representing the percentage of scheduled time that equipment was available for production.
Calculated performance component of OEE for this operation, representing actual production speed versus ideal speed.
Calculated quality component of OEE for this operation, representing the percentage of good output versus total output produced.
Sequential operation identifier within the production order routing. Typically a 4-digit numeric code representing the step in the manufacturing process.
Current lifecycle status of the manufacturing operation indicating its execution state in the production workflow.
Financial posting date when this confirmation was recorded in the ERP system for inventory and cost accounting purposes.
Indicates whether this operation output requires quality inspection before release to inventory or next operation.
Indicates whether this confirmation has been reversed or cancelled due to error correction or process adjustment.
Standardized code explaining why this confirmation was reversed, if applicable. Used for process improvement and error tracking.
Indicates whether this confirmation represents a rework operation to correct defects from a previous production run.
Planned completion date and time for this operation as determined by production scheduling or MES system.
Planned start date and time for this operation as determined by production scheduling or MES system.
Production shift identifier during which this operation was executed (e.g., SHIFT_1, DAY, NIGHT). Used for shift performance analysis.
Identifier of the originating system that created this confirmation record (SAP PP, Siemens Opcenter MES, or manual entry).
Standard unit of measure for the confirmed quantities (e.g., KG for kilograms, EA for each, LT for liters). Aligns with material master UOM.
Standardized code explaining any significant variance between planned and actual quantities or times. Used for root cause analysis.
Business identifier for the work order assigned to this manufacturing operation. Externally visible reference used across shop floor systems.
Unique identifier for the production line. Primary key for the production line master record.
FK to finance.cost_center
Foreign key linking to sustainability.energy_certificate. Business justification: Energy certificates certify renewable energy for a line; linking enables line‑level energy compliance tracking.

Foreign key linking to manufacturing.manufacturing_facility. Business justification: Production line belongs to a specific manufacturing facility; replace generic facility reference with direct link to manufacturing_facility.
Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Line supervisor drives OEE, quality and shift planning; plant experts expect a dedicated supervisor link per line.
Indicates whether this production line handles products containing allergens. Critical for cross-contamination prevention and regulatory compliance.

Foreign key linking to logistics.carrier. Business justification: CARRIER_ASSIGNMENT: Supply plan assigns a primary carrier for the planned shipments, required for cost and SLA calculations.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Cost allocation of each supply plan to a finance cost center for budgeting and variance analysis; planners routinely charge production plans to cost centers.

Foreign key linking to supply.demand_plan. Business justification: A supply plan is derived from a specific demand plan; linking plan to demand_plan captures the parent‑child relationship and enables traceability of plan origins.
Reference to the distribution center or warehouse location for which this supply plan applies.
Reference to the supply planner or demand planner responsible for this supply plan.

Foreign key linking to logistics.lane. Business justification: TRANSPORT_PLANNING: Supply plan defines the transportation lane for moving goods; planners need lane_id to generate accurate movement schedules.
Reference to the manufacturing plant or production facility where the SKU will be produced.

Foreign key linking to supply.planning_run. Business justification: A supply plan is generated as part of a planning run; adding planning_run_id creates the proper parent link and allows removal of the redundant planning_run_code attribute.
Foreign key linking to promotion.promotion_event. Business justification: REQUIRED: S&OP supply planning must align production/replenishment with upcoming promotion events to meet forecasted uplift.

Foreign key linking to research.rd_project. Business justification: Business process: Supply Planning for a new product requires linking each supply_plan to the rd_project that defines the product, ensuring capacity and material plans reflect R&D intent.
Foreign key linking to regulatory.registration. Business justification: Supply planning must avoid producing or allocating unregistered SKUs; registration link validates plan feasibility.
Reference to the specific SKU for which this supply plan is created.
Reference to the external supplier if the supply source is external procurement or contract manufacturing.
Reference to the source location (plant or DC) if the supply source is a transfer from another internal location.
Foreign key linking to customer.trade_account. Business justification: REQUIRED: Store‑specific supply plan ties replenishment to the owning trade_account; essential for execution and KPI reporting.
The quantity of the SKU that is available to promise to customers for delivery during the planning period, based on projected supply and committed demand.
Indicates whether the supply plan is constrained by production or distribution capacity limitations.
The timestamp when this supply plan record was first created in the system.
The quantity of the SKU that can be promised to customers considering both current inventory and planned production capacity.
The forecasted demand quantity for this SKU at this location during the planning period, used as input to the supply planning process.
The date when this supply plan was executed or committed, triggering downstream production orders or purchase requisitions.
The timestamp when this supply plan record was last updated or modified.
The number of days required from order release to receipt, including production time, procurement time, or transfer time.
Indicates whether the supply plan is constrained by raw material or component availability.
Free-text notes or comments from the supply planner regarding assumptions, constraints, or special considerations for this supply plan.
The current lifecycle status of the supply plan record indicating its approval and execution state.
Classification of the supply plan indicating whether it is constrained by capacity and material availability, unconstrained (infinite capacity), a scenario analysis, or a simulation.
The date when the production order or purchase order should be released to meet the planned receipt date, accounting for lead times.
The quantity of the SKU planned to be produced at the specified plant during the planning period.
The date when the planned supply quantity is expected to be received or available at the destination location.
The quantity of the SKU planned to be replenished or transferred to the distribution center during the planning period.
The time granularity or bucket size used for this supply plan (daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly aggregation).
The organizational planning group or team responsible for managing supply planning for this SKU or location combination.
The end date of the planning horizon covered by this supply plan record.
The start date of the planning horizon covered by this supply plan record.
The projected on-hand inventory balance at the end of the planning period after accounting for planned supply and demand.
The target safety stock quantity maintained as a buffer against demand variability and supply uncertainty for this SKU at this location.
The name or identifier of the source system from which this supply plan record originated (e.g., SAP IBP, Oracle Cloud Supply Chain).
A calculated risk score indicating the likelihood of supply disruption or shortage for this SKU at this location, based on supplier reliability, lead time variability, and demand volatility.
The source from which the supply will be obtained: internal production, external procurement from suppliers, transfer from another location, or contract manufacturing.
Indicates whether the supply plan is constrained by transportation or logistics capacity limitations.
The unit of measure for the planned quantities (e.g., cases, pallets, kilograms, liters).
Version identifier for the supply plan, enabling tracking of plan iterations and scenario comparisons (e.g., baseline, consensus, committed).
Unique identifier for the planning exception record. Primary key for the planning exception entity.
Reference to the supply planner or demand planner assigned to resolve this exception.
Reference to the SKU affected by this planning exception.
Reference to the plant, distribution center, or location where the planning exception occurred.
Reference to the user who last modified the planning exception record.

Classification of the recommended action type for resolving the exception. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: expedite_order|cancel_order|increase_production|decrease_production|transfer_stock|adjust_forecast|override_plan — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Indicates whether the exception was automatically resolved by the system without planner intervention.
Estimated financial impact of the exception if not resolved, expressed in the reporting currency.
Type of supply chain constraint that contributed to the planning exception.
