Three-letter ISO currency code for the business impact amount.
The forecasted demand quantity for the affected SKU-location during the exception period.
Indicates whether the exception was escalated to management or cross-functional teams for resolution.
The organizational level to which the exception was escalated, if applicable.
The date when the planning exception was identified or when the exception condition is projected to occur.
Additional free-text notes or comments related to the planning exception for planner reference.
Business-facing unique exception number assigned to this planning exception for tracking and reference purposes.
The magnitude of the exception expressed as a quantity (e.g., shortage quantity, excess quantity, unmet demand quantity).
Number of times this type of exception has occurred for the same SKU-location combination within a defined time window.
Severity classification of the planning exception indicating the urgency and business impact of the issue.

The precise timestamp when the planning exception was detected and recorded by the IBP system.

Classification of the planning exception indicating the nature of the supply planning issue. OOS Risk (Out of Stock Risk), Excess Inventory, Late Replenishment, Unmet Demand, Capacity Breach, or Safety Stock Breach.
The calculated gap between demand and supply that triggered the exception (positive for shortage, negative for excess).

The planning group or team responsible for managing exceptions for this SKU-location combination.
The specific date within the planning horizon where the exception condition manifests.
Reference to the IBP planning run or DRP execution run that generated this exception.
Calculated priority score used to rank exceptions in the planner workbench, based on severity, business impact, and urgency.
The projected inventory balance at the time of the exception, used to assess the severity of stock-out or excess inventory conditions.
System-generated or planner-defined recommended action to resolve the planning exception.
The date when the planning exception was marked as resolved or closed.
The elapsed time in hours from exception detection to resolution, used for performance tracking.
Free-text notes documenting the actions taken to resolve the exception and the outcome.
The precise timestamp when the planning exception was marked as resolved or closed.
High-level categorization of the root cause that triggered the planning exception.
reference: Supply Chain Root Cause Analysis Framework

description: Detailed description of the root cause analysis findings for the planning exception.
The target safety stock level for the SKU-location combination at the time of the exception.
The source system that generated the planning exception (e.g., SAP IBP, TradeEdge, internal planning engine).
The planned supply quantity (production or replenishment) for the affected SKU-location during the exception period.
The unit of measure for the exception quantity (e.g., EA for each, CS for case, PAL for pallet).

Origin of the input data used for the planning run.
Total elapsed time of the run measured in minutes.

Category of planning activity performed in the run (e.g., demand, supply, inventory, S&OP, optimization).
Code representing the scenario (e.g., baseline, best‑case, worst‑case) used for this run.

True if the run completed without errors; otherwise False.

business_glossary_term: Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) Cycle ID
description: Unique identifier for the S&OP/IBP planning cycle instance. Primary key.
reference: APICS Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Model

description: Identifier of the employee responsible for orchestrating and governing this S&OP cycle (typically the Demand Planning Manager or S&OP Manager).
Identifier of the executive sponsor who chairs the executive S&OP meeting and provides final sign-off (typically VP of Supply Chain or COO).
Identifier of the user who last modified this S&OP cycle record.
Identifier of the lead supply planner responsible for the supply review phase of this cycle.
The total baseline demand volume (in units) across all SKUs for the planning horizon at the start of this cycle.
The total consensus demand volume (in units) across all SKUs after demand review adjustments.
The total constrained supply volume (in units) that can be delivered given capacity and material constraints.
The timestamp when this S&OP cycle record was first created in the system.
Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the cycle for external reference and system integration (e.g., 'SOP-2024-01', 'IBP-Q1-24').
The date when this S&OP cycle is scheduled to complete and be locked (typically before the start of the planning month).
The date when this S&OP cycle was locked and finalized.
Indicates whether this S&OP cycle has been locked and no further changes are permitted (True if locked, False if still open for edits).
Business-friendly name or label for the S&OP cycle (e.g., 'January 2024 S&OP Cycle', 'Q1 FY2024 IBP').
reference: APICS Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Model

description: General free-text notes or comments about this S&OP cycle, including special circumstances, deviations from standard process, or other relevant context.

Current phase of the S&OP cycle: statistical_forecast (initial statistical forecast generation), demand_review (demand planning team review), supply_review (supply planning team review), pre_sop (pre-S&OP reconciliation meeting), executive_sop (executive S&OP decision meeting), closed (cycle completed and locked).
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: The date when this S&OP cycle officially begins (typically the first day of the cycle month).

The cadence or type of S&OP cycle: monthly (standard monthly cadence), quarterly (quarterly review), annual (annual planning), rolling (continuous rolling horizon), event_driven (triggered by specific business events).
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Indicates whether demand consensus was achieved during the demand review phase (True if consensus reached, False otherwise).
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Target date by which the demand review phase must be completed.
The date when the executive sponsor formally approved the S&OP plan for this cycle.
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Indicates whether the executive S&OP meeting approved the plan (True if approved, False if rejected or pending).
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Free-text notes or comments from the executive sponsor regarding the approval decision, including any conditions or action items.
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Scheduled date for the executive S&OP meeting where senior leadership reviews and approves the plan.
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: The fiscal period (month number) within the fiscal year (e.g., 1 for January, 12 for December).
The fiscal year to which this planning cycle belongs (e.g., 2024).
The number of months at the start of the planning horizon that are frozen and not subject to change (typically 0-3 months).
Free-text field capturing the key business assumptions underlying this S&OP cycle (e.g., promotional plans, market trends, supply constraints, new product launches).
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Free-text field documenting the key risks identified during this S&OP cycle (e.g., supplier reliability, demand volatility, capacity constraints).
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: The timestamp when this S&OP cycle record was last updated.
Free-text field describing the mitigation actions agreed upon to address identified risks and supply gaps.
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Status of the current cycle phase: not_started (phase has not begun), in_progress (phase is actively underway), completed (phase finished and approved), on_hold (phase temporarily paused), cancelled (phase or cycle cancelled).
The number of months into the future that this S&OP cycle plans (e.g., 18 months, 24 months).
The target month for which this S&OP cycle is planning demand and supply (typically the first day of the planning month).
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Scheduled date for the pre-S&OP reconciliation meeting where demand and supply teams align on recommendations.
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: Target date by which the statistical forecast phase must be completed.
Indicates whether supply consensus was achieved during the supply review phase (True if consensus reached, False otherwise).
reference: APICS Sales and Operations Planning Best Practices

description: The total supply gap (in units) representing the difference between consensus demand and constrained supply (positive indicates shortfall, negative indicates surplus).
Target date by which the supply review phase must be completed.
Unique identifier for the supply replenishment order record. Primary key for this entity.
Foreign key linking to logistics.carrier_contract. Business justification: CONTRACT_COMPLIANCE: Each replenishment order is governed by a carrier contract; needed for rate and penalty enforcement.
Identifier of the logistics carrier or transportation provider assigned to execute this replenishment shipment.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Replenishment orders incur expenses that must be tracked against the responsible cost center for expense reporting and internal charge‑backs.
Identifier of the supply network node to which inventory will be delivered (distribution center, warehouse, or retail location).
Identifier of the DRP execution run that generated this replenishment order, used for traceability and audit.

Foreign key linking to quality.inspection_lot. Business justification: Regulatory traceability requires linking each replenishment order to its inspection lot for recall and safety reporting; experts expect this FK for product safety audits.
Foreign key linking to logistics.lane. Business justification: ORDER_EXECUTION: Replenishment order execution follows a specific lane; lane_id links order to transportation routing.
Identifier of the physical shipment record associated with this replenishment order once released for execution.
Identifier of the system user or automated process that created this replenishment order record.
Identifier of the supply network node from which inventory will be shipped (plant, distribution center, or warehouse).
Foreign key linking to promotion.promotion_event. Business justification: REQUIRED: Replenishment orders are often generated to satisfy demand generated by a specific promotion event.
Foreign key linking to regulatory.registration. Business justification: Regulatory compliance verification before order release ensures SKU has active registration; essential for legal shipment.
Identifier of the product SKU being replenished through this order.
Actual date the goods were received at the destination location.
Actual date the shipment departed from the source location.
ATP quantity at the source location at the time the replenishment order was created, used to validate supply availability.
Reason code or description explaining why the replenishment order was cancelled, if applicable.
Quantity of the SKU confirmed for shipment by the source location, may differ from requested quantity due to supply constraints.
Date and time when this replenishment order record was first created in the system.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this order.
Date and time when the DRP execution run that generated this order was executed.
Forecasted demand quantity at the destination location that drove the replenishment calculation.
Date and time when this replenishment order record was last modified in the system.
Total cost associated with this replenishment order, including product cost, transportation cost, and handling fees.
Free-text notes or special instructions related to this replenishment order, such as handling requirements or routing constraints.
Current execution status of the replenishment order in the supply chain workflow.
Classification of the replenishment order lifecycle stage: planned (system-generated recommendation), firmed (manually confirmed but not released), or released (committed for execution).
Target date for goods receipt at the destination location, accounting for transit lead time.
Target date for shipment departure from the source location as calculated by the DRP engine.
Priority classification for order fulfillment, typically driven by stock-out risk, customer service level, or strategic importance.
Actual quantity of the SKU received at the destination location, captured at goods receipt.
Business-facing unique order number for the replenishment order, used for tracking and reference across systems and communications.
Quantity of the SKU requested for replenishment as calculated by the DRP engine or demand planner.
Indicates whether this replenishment order was triggered by inventory falling below safety stock threshold at the destination location.
Actual quantity of the SKU shipped from the source location, captured at dispatch.
Planned number of days for goods to travel from source to destination location.
Primary mode of transportation planned or used for this replenishment shipment.

Unit of measure for all quantity fields in this order (EA=Each, CS=Case, PL=Pallet, KG=Kilogram, LB=Pound, L=Liter, GAL=Gallon). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|CS|PL|EA|KG|LB|L|GAL — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Unique surrogate identifier for each immutable consent status change event record in the audit log. Primary key of the consent_event table.

Reference to the marketing campaign or trade promotion that triggered or was associated with this consent collection event. Enables campaign-level consent acquisition analytics and Trade Promotion Management (TPM) reporting.
reference: Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud; GDPR Article 13

description: Reference to the parent consent record that this event modifies. Links the event to the current state of the consumer's consent agreement managed in the consent master table.

Reference identifier of the formal Data Subject Access Request (DSAR), right-to-erasure request, or opt-out request that triggered this consent event. Populated when change_trigger is 'regulatory_request'. Links the event to the formal rights management workflow.

Identifier of the human agent (e.g., call center representative, CRM user) or automated system that processed and recorded this consent change event. Supports accountability tracing required by GDPR Article 5(2).
reference: GDPR Article 5(2); CCPA Section 1798.120; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.jurisdiction. Business justification: Regulatory reporting of consent changes must reference the jurisdiction that governs the consent.
Reference to the specific preference center or consent management portal instance through which this consent event was captured. Supports multi-brand and multi-region preference center deployments.
reference: GDPR Article 7; CCPA Section 1798.120; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud

description: Reference to the consent event that reversed or corrected this event, if applicable. Populated when event_status is 'reversed'. Maintains the immutable audit chain while flagging erroneous records.

Unique identifier of the web or mobile application session during which the consent event was captured. Enables cross-referencing with session analytics and digital behavior logs for audit trail completeness.
reference: GDPR Article 7; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud

description: Reference to the consumer whose consent status changed. Identifies the data subject for GDPR/CCPA audit trail purposes.

Code identifying the Consumer Goods brand or product line in whose context the consent was collected (e.g., a specific personal care or household brand). Supports brand-level consent segmentation and multi-brand CRM programs.
reference: Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud; GDPR Article 13

description: The interaction channel through which the consent change was submitted or processed. Supports channel-level compliance reporting and consumer journey analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: web|mobile_app|call_center|in_store|email|postal|crm_agent|api — promote to reference product]
reference: GDPR Article 7; CCPA Section 1798.120; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud

description: The initiating cause of the consent status change. 'consumer_action' = consumer explicitly acted; 'system_expiry' = automated expiry rule fired; 'regulatory_request' = GDPR/CCPA erasure or opt-out request; 'admin_override' = internal compliance team action; 'data_import' = bulk migration or integration import.

The date on which the consent granted in this event is scheduled to expire and require renewal. Supports automated consent refresh workflows and ensures time-limited consent is not used beyond its valid period.
reference: GDPR Article 7; ICO Guidance on Consent; ISO/IEC 29101

description: ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) of the language in which the consent notice was presented to the consumer (e.g., 'en', 'en-US', 'fr-FR'). Supports multilingual compliance documentation.

Standardized code identifying the specific processing purpose for which consent was changed (e.g., MARKETING_EMAIL, PERSONALIZATION, ANALYTICS, THIRD_PARTY_SHARING, LOYALTY_PROGRAM). Aligns with the consent purpose taxonomy defined under GDPR Article 5(1)(b) and CCPA categories.
reference: GDPR Article 5(1)(b); CCPA Section 1798.100; IAB TCF 2.0

description: Human-readable name of the processing purpose for which consent was changed. Provides business-friendly label alongside the consent_purpose_code for reporting and consumer-facing disclosures.
reference: GDPR Article 13; CCPA Section 1798.100; IAB TCF 2.0

description: Verbatim or summarized text of the consent notice or opt-in/opt-out statement presented to the consumer at the time of this event. Immutable snapshot stored for evidentiary purposes under GDPR Article 7(1) and CCPA audit requirements.

Version identifier of the consent notice, privacy policy, or terms document that was presented to the consumer at the time of this consent event. Required to demonstrate that consent was informed under GDPR Article 7(1).

Indicates whether this consent grant was confirmed via a double opt-in mechanism (True), where the consumer confirmed their consent through a secondary verification step such as an email confirmation link. Relevant for email marketing compliance.
Date and time when the consumer completed the double opt-in confirmation step (e.g., clicked the email verification link). Null if double_opt_in_flag is False or not applicable.

Processing status of this consent event record. 'processed' = successfully applied to the consumer's consent profile; 'pending' = awaiting confirmation (e.g., double opt-in); 'failed' = processing error; 'reversed' = event was reversed due to error correction.
reference: GDPR Article 7; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud; ISO/IEC 29101

description: Precise date and time (with timezone offset) when the consent status change event occurred. This is the authoritative business event time used for GDPR Article 7 and CCPA compliance audits, distinct from the record ingestion timestamp.

Discriminator classifying the kind of consent change event. 'grant' = consumer actively provided consent; 'withdraw' = consumer revoked consent; 'update' = scope or preferences modified; 'expire' = consent lapsed due to time limit; 'regulatory_erasure' = right-to-be-forgotten request; 'system_expiry' = automated system-driven expiry. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: grant|withdraw|update|expire|regulatory_erasure|system_expiry — promote to reference product]

IP address of the consumer's device at the time of the consent event submission. Captured as evidentiary proof of consent origin for GDPR Article 7 compliance. May be considered PII in certain jurisdictions.
reference: GDPR Article 7; GDPR Recital 30; CCPA Section 1798.140

description: GDPR Article 6 lawful basis under which personal data processing is authorized at the time of this event. 'consent' is the primary basis for marketing; other bases apply to operational processing. Required for GDPR Article 30 Records of Processing Activities.
reference: GDPR Article 6; GDPR Article 30; ICO Guidance on Lawful Basis

description: Indicates whether the consumer was identified as a minor (under 16 years for GDPR, under 13 for COPPA) at the time of this consent event. Triggers parental consent verification workflows and restricts certain processing activities.
reference: GDPR Article 8; COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act); CCPA

description: The consent status of the consumer immediately after this event was processed. Together with prior_consent_status, provides the complete state transition record for regulatory audit purposes.

Free-text field for compliance officers or CRM agents to record additional context, observations, or exceptions related to this consent event. Not used for structured data; intended for human-readable audit annotations.

Indicates whether the resulting consent status after this event represents an active opt-in (True) or opt-out/withdrawal (False). Provides a simple boolean signal for downstream marketing suppression lists and CRM segmentation.
reference: GDPR Article 7; CCPA Section 1798.120; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud

description: Indicates whether parental or guardian consent was obtained for this consent event, applicable when minor_flag is True. Required for GDPR Article 8 and COPPA compliance for processing data of minors.

The consent status of the consumer immediately before this event was processed. Captured as an immutable snapshot to enable full before/after audit trail required by GDPR Article 7 compliance reviews.

Name or identifier of the operational system that processed and recorded this consent event (e.g., Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud, CRM Portal, Preference Center API). Provides system-level audit trail for data lineage.
reference: GDPR Article 30; CCPA Section 1798.100; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud

description: Indicates whether the consumer has consented to automated profiling and personalization activities (True = profiling consented; False = profiling not consented or withdrawn). Relevant for GDPR Article 22 automated decision-making compliance.
reference: GDPR Article 22; CCPA Section 1798.120; FTC Act Section 5

description: Reference identifier or document path pointing to the stored evidence of consent (e.g., signed form scan, recorded call reference, screenshot archive, Veeva Vault document ID). Supports GDPR Article 7(1) burden-of-proof requirements.

Date and time when this consent event record was first ingested and persisted in the data platform (Silver Layer). Distinct from event_timestamp which captures the real-world business event time. Used for data lineage and SLA monitoring.
reference: GDPR Article 30; ISO 8601; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer

description: The specific data protection regulatory framework under which this consent event is governed and must be reported. Enables framework-specific compliance reporting and audit filtering.
reference: GDPR; CCPA Section 1798.120; UK GDPR; PIPEDA; LGPD

description: The web URL or deep-link of the page, form, or digital touchpoint where the consumer submitted the consent change (e.g., preference center URL, checkout page, registration form). Provides evidence of the consent collection point for GDPR Article 7 accountability.
reference: GDPR Article 7(1); CCPA Section 1798.100; IAB TCF 2.0

description: Indicates whether this consent event includes or affects the consumer's consent for sharing their personal data with third-party partners, retailers, or data brokers (True = sharing consented; False = sharing not consented or withdrawn).
reference: GDPR Article 6; CCPA Section 1798.120; FTC Act Section 5

description: Browser or application user-agent string captured at the time of the consent event. Provides technical evidence of the device and browser environment used when consent was given, supporting GDPR Article 7 proof-of-consent requirements.

Standardized code capturing the consumer's stated reason for withdrawing consent (e.g., TOO_FREQUENT, NOT_RELEVANT, PRIVACY_CONCERN, UNSUBSCRIBE_ALL). Null for non-withdrawal events. Supports consumer experience analytics and suppression management.
reference: GDPR Article 7(3); CCPA Section 1798.120; Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud

description: Free-text description provided by the consumer or agent explaining the reason for consent withdrawal. Supplements withdrawal_reason_code with verbatim consumer feedback for qualitative analysis.

Unique surrogate identifier for each consent record in the Consumer Goods consumer privacy system. Primary key for the consent_record data product, serving as the SSOT for GDPR Article 7 and CCPA compliance audits.

Reference to the marketing or re-consent campaign that prompted this consent record creation or update. Enables campaign-level consent conversion tracking and supports Trade Promotion Management (TPM) and consumer engagement analytics.
reference: GDPR Article 7; FTC Advertising and Labeling Guidelines

description: Reference to the distribution or engagement channel (e.g., DTC e-commerce, retail loyalty, mobile app) through which the consumer relationship was established and consent was captured. Supports channel-level consent analytics.

Reference identifier of the Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) or right-to-erasure request that triggered a consent status change, if applicable. Links consent changes to formal regulatory requests for audit traceability under GDPR Articles 15-22.
reference: GDPR Article 15; GDPR Article 17; GDPR Article 21; CCPA Section 1798.105

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.jurisdiction. Business justification: Data privacy compliance mandates mapping each consent record to its governing jurisdiction for regulatory reporting.

Reference to the loyalty program associated with this consent record, if the consumer is a loyalty program member. Consent for loyalty program data processing is tracked separately from general marketing consent.

Reference to the Consumer Goods brand for which this consent was captured. Enables brand-level consent reporting and ensures that consent granted for one brand is not incorrectly applied to another brand within the same corporate portfolio.
reference: GDPR Article 7; CCPA Section 1798.100; FTC Advertising and Labeling Guidelines

description: Reference to the consumer profile record for whom this consent record applies. Links the consent record to the consumer master in the CRM/DTC system (Salesforce Consumer Goods Cloud).

Channel or mechanism through which the consumer's consent was captured. Identifies whether consent was obtained via a web form, mobile app, in-store interaction, call center agent, paper form, or email link. Required for GDPR proof-of-consent obligations.
reference: GDPR Article 7(1); GDPR Recital 42; CCPA Section 1798.100

description: Exact date and time (with timezone offset) when the consumer's consent action was recorded in the system. This is the principal business event timestamp for the consent record and is immutable once set. Required for GDPR Article 7 audit trail.

The business reason or event that triggered the most recent change to the consent status. Distinguishes consumer-initiated changes from system-driven expirations, administrative overrides, legal requests (e.g., right to erasure), or re-consent campaigns.
reference: GDPR Article 7(3); GDPR Article 17; CCPA Section 1798.105; ISO 29101

description: ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) of the language in which the consent notice was presented to the consumer (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de', 'es-MX'). Required to confirm consent was given in an intelligible form per GDPR Article 7.
reference: GDPR Article 7(2); GDPR Recital 42; ISO 639-1; ISO 3166-1

description: Reference identifier or URL pointing to the stored proof-of-consent artifact (e.g., screenshot, signed form scan, call recording reference, Veeva Vault document ID). Supports GDPR Article 7(1) obligation to demonstrate that consent was given.
reference: GDPR Article 7(1); Veeva Vault (Quality Documents); ISO 27001

description: Defines the breadth of the consent grant — whether it applies globally across all Consumer Goods brands and products, is restricted to a specific brand, product category, or a single campaign. Enables granular consent management across the product portfolio.

reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Multi-Level BOM Explosion; MRP (Material Requirements Planning)

description: The quantity of the component required to produce one unit of the parent SKU at the base quantity defined in the BOM header. Satisfies TRANSACTION_LINE LINE_QUANTITY category. Supports MRP and COGS calculation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM/PP Module - BOM Component Quantity (MENGE); MRP (Material Requirements Planning)

description: The expected percentage of this component that will be lost or wasted during the manufacturing process. Used to inflate the planned component quantity in MRP runs and COGS calculations. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 2.5 = 2.5%).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Component Scrap (AUSSS); GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice)

description: The document number or reference identifier for the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) associated with this hazardous component. Links to the SDS stored in Veeva Vault or the document management system for regulatory compliance.
reference: OSHA HazCom Standard 29 CFR 1910.1200; EU REACH Regulation; Veeva Vault Quality Documents; SDS (Safety Data Sheet)

description: Identifier for the operational system of record from which this BOM line was sourced (e.g., SAP_S4HANA, ORACLE_ERP). Supports data lineage tracking and multi-system reconciliation in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Data Lineage Standards; SAP S/4HANA; Oracle Cloud ERP

description: The designated warehouse storage location or bin where this component is staged for production consumption. Used by WMS and MES for material staging, goods issue, and FEFO/FIFO inventory management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA WM Module - Storage Location (LGORT); Blue Yonder WMS; FEFO (First Expired First Out); FIFO (First In First Out)

description: The unit of measure for the required quantity of the component (e.g., KG, L, EA, M, G). Must align with the component material master UOM. Satisfies TRANSACTION_LINE LINE_VALUE_OR_RESULT category (measurement dimension).
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - Base Unit of Measure (MEINS); GS1 UN/ECE Recommendation 20

description: The probability (expressed as a percentage, 0–100) that this alternative component will actually be used in production. Used by MRP to calculate weighted component requirements across alternative item groups.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module - Usage Probability (EWAHR)

description: The date from which this BOM line is effective and should be included in production and MRP planning. Supports date-effective BOM management for product reformulations and packaging changes.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - BOM Valid From Date (DATUV); PLM (Product Lifecycle Management)

description: The date after which this BOM line is no longer effective and should be excluded from production and MRP planning. Null indicates the line is open-ended with no planned expiry.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - BOM Valid To Date (DATUB); PLM (Product Lifecycle Management)

description: Unique identifier for the pack hierarchy record. Primary key.
Reference to the SKU for which this pack hierarchy is defined. Links to the product master.
The date and time when this pack hierarchy record was first created in the system.
The total number of consumer units (eaches) contained in this packaging level. For a case containing 6 inner packs of 12 eaches, this would be 72.
Indicates whether this packaging level is designed as a retail-ready display unit that can be placed directly on the sales floor without unpacking.
The 13-digit EAN barcode identifier for this packaging level, used internationally for consumer units.
The date on which this pack hierarchy configuration is no longer valid, supporting packaging changes and product lifecycle management.
The date from which this pack hierarchy configuration becomes active and valid for use in operations.
The total weight of the packaging at this level including product and packaging materials, measured in kilograms.
The GS1 Global Trade Item Number assigned to this packaging level. May be GTIN-8, GTIN-12 (UPC), GTIN-13 (EAN), or GTIN-14 (case/pallet).
The height dimension of the packaging at this level, measured in centimeters.
The number of layers stacked on a pallet (Hi in Ti-Hi configuration). Used for pallet configuration and warehouse planning.
The packaging level within the hierarchy: each (consumer unit), inner pack (multi-pack), case (shipper), display unit (retail-ready), pallet (full pallet), or layer (pallet layer).
The length dimension of the packaging at this level, measured in centimeters.
The maximum number of units of this packaging level that can be safely stacked vertically.
The date and time when this pack hierarchy record was last modified or updated.
The minimum order quantity required for this packaging level, used in order processing and trade promotion planning.
The weight of the product content only at this level, excluding packaging materials, measured in kilograms.
Indicates whether this packaging level can be ordered by customers or retailers through EDI or other ordering systems.
The current lifecycle status of this pack hierarchy configuration: active (in use), inactive (temporarily suspended), pending (awaiting approval), or discontinued (permanently retired).
The primary material used for packaging at this level: corrugated cardboard, plastic, wood, metal, composite, or shrink wrap.
The type of pallet used for this packaging level: standard (48x40 inches), euro (1200x800 mm), block, custom, half, or quarter pallet.
The number of units from the next lower hierarchy level contained in this level (e.g., 12 eaches per inner pack, 6 inner packs per case).
Indicates whether the packaging material at this level is recyclable according to local recycling standards.
The percentage of recycled material content in the packaging at this level, supporting sustainability reporting.
Indicates whether this packaging level is suitable for direct shipment to customers or distribution centers.
Indicates whether this packaging level can be safely stacked on top of similar units during storage and transportation.
The weight of the packaging materials only at this level, excluding product content, measured in kilograms.
The number of cases or units per layer on a pallet (Ti in Ti-Hi configuration). Used for pallet configuration and warehouse planning.
The 12-digit UPC barcode identifier for this packaging level, primarily used in North America for consumer units.
The cubic volume of the packaging at this level, measured in cubic centimeters. Used for warehouse slotting and transportation cube optimization.
The width dimension of the packaging at this level, measured in centimeters.
Unique surrogate identifier for the Bill of Materials (BOM) header record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: BOM release requires employee approval; tracked for manufacturing release and change control.

Reference to the manufacturing plant or production site that owns this BOM. BOMs in SAP are plant-specific; the same material may have different BOMs per plant reflecting local sourcing or production capabilities.
Reference to the finished good or semi-finished SKU for which this BOM is defined. Links to the product master (material master in SAP). A single SKU may have multiple BOMs of different types.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module — Material Master (MARA/MARC)

description: Alternative BOM identifier (SAP STLAL) allowing multiple BOM variants for the same material and plant combination. Used to manage seasonal formulations, regional variants, or cost-optimized alternatives within the same SKU.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — Alternative BOM (STLAL)

description: Date on which this BOM was formally approved for production use. Part of the GMP and PLM audit trail. Required for regulatory submissions and quality management documentation.
reference: ISO 22716 GMP; ISO 9001 Section 7.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault PLM

description: The reference quantity of the finished or semi-finished material for which the BOM component quantities are specified. All component quantities in BOM line items are expressed relative to this base quantity. Typically 1 or 100 in CPG manufacturing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Header Base Quantity (STKO-BMENG); GMP ISO 22716

description: Unit of measure for the BOM base quantity (e.g., KG, L, EA, G). Defines the unit in which the finished good is expressed for component ratio calculations. Aligns with SAP base unit of measure (MARA-MEINS) and GS1 unit codes.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module — Base Unit of Measure (MARA-MEINS); GS1 Global Standards

description: SAP BOM category indicating the object type the BOM is assigned to. 'material' is the standard category for product BOMs in CPG/FMCG. 'equipment' and 'functional_location' apply to plant maintenance BOMs. Aligns with SAP STKO-STLTY.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Category (STKO-STLTY)

description: Human-readable description of the BOM, typically including the product name, formulation variant, and intended use. Used in PLM, engineering change orders, and regulatory documentation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Header Text; Veeva Vault PLM

description: Indicates the level of the BOM in a multi-level product structure. Level 0 is the finished good, level 1 represents direct components, level 2 represents sub-components, etc. Used for multi-level BOM explosion in MRP and costing roll-ups.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — Multi-Level BOM Explosion (CS12); MRP (Material Requirements Planning)

description: Externally-known BOM document number as assigned in SAP S/4HANA PP/MM (e.g., SAP BOM header number). This is the business-facing identifier used in PLM, procurement, and manufacturing communications.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — CS01/CS02 BOM Header

description: Classifies the purpose of the BOM. 'production' is used for manufacturing execution (MRP/MES), 'costing' for COGS and standard cost roll-up, 'engineering' for R&D and NPD design, 'sales' for variant configuration, 'configurable' for multi-variant BOMs. Aligns with SAP BOM usage (STLAL).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Usage (STLAL); GMP ISO 22716

description: Engineering Change Number (ECN) or Engineering Change Order (ECO) reference that authorized the creation or modification of this BOM version. Provides traceability from BOM changes back to the formal change management process in PLM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — Engineering Change Management (ECM); ISO 9001 Section 8.3; Veeva Vault PLM

description: Total number of active component line items in this BOM. Provides a quick indicator of BOM complexity and is used in BOM completeness validation checks during PLM review and quality audits.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Item Count; ISO 9001 Section 8.3; PLM

description: Indicates whether this BOM is relevant for product costing (COGS calculation and standard cost roll-up). 'relevant' means the BOM is included in cost estimates, 'not_relevant' excludes it, 'conditional' applies under specific costing scenarios. Critical for financial reporting and EBITDA analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module — Product Costing (CO-PC); COGS; SOX Financial Reporting

description: Timestamp when this BOM record was first created in the source system (SAP S/4HANA). Provides the audit trail creation marker required for GMP, SOX, and ISO 9001 compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — ERDAT/ERZET; ISO 9001 Section 7.5; SOX; GMP ISO 22716

description: Indicates whether this BOM has been flagged for deletion in SAP. A deletion flag marks the BOM as logically deleted without physically removing the record, preserving audit history. Aligns with SAP STKO-LOEKZ.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Deletion Flag (STKO-LOEKZ); SOX Compliance

description: The date from which this BOM version is valid and can be used for production planning, MRP, and costing. Supports time-phased BOM management for seasonal reformulations, ingredient substitutions, or regulatory-driven changes.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Valid From Date (STKO-DATUV); ISO 9001 Section 7.5

description: The date until which this BOM version is valid. Null indicates an open-ended validity. Used to manage BOM version transitions during reformulations, regulatory updates, or product discontinuations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Valid To Date (STKO-DATUB); ISO 9001 Section 7.5

description: R&D or regulatory formulation code that uniquely identifies the product formula associated with this BOM. Links the manufacturing BOM to the R&D formulation record in Veeva Vault or PLM system. Critical for INCI ingredient declaration and regulatory submissions.
reference: Veeva Vault PLM — Formulation Record; INCI (International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients); FDA 21 CFR; EU REACH Regulation

description: Indicates whether this BOM has been validated as compliant with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. Required for health, hygiene, and personal care products. Compliance is verified during quality review before BOM activation.
reference: ISO 22716 (GMP for Cosmetics); FDA 21 CFR Part 111; GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice)

description: Indicates whether this BOM supports variant configuration, allowing different component selections based on product characteristics (e.g., fragrance variant, pack size). Used for configurable products in CPG where a single BOM covers multiple SKU variants.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/SD Module — Variant Configuration (LO-VC); PLM

description: Indicates whether this BOM represents a phantom assembly — a logical grouping of components that does not physically exist as a stocked item but is used to simplify BOM structures. Phantom assemblies are exploded through in MRP without generating production orders.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — Phantom Assembly (MARC-LGPRO); MRP

description: User ID or name of the person who last modified this BOM record. Part of the change audit trail required for GMP, engineering change management, and SOX compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — AENAM; ISO 9001 Section 7.5; SOX; GMP ISO 22716

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this BOM record in the source system. Used for incremental data loading, change detection, and audit trail maintenance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — AEDAT/AEZET; ISO 9001 Section 7.5; SOX; GMP ISO 22716

description: Minimum lot size for which this BOM is valid. BOMs can be lot-size dependent in process manufacturing, where component quantities vary based on batch size. Used in conjunction with lot_size_to to define the valid production quantity range.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — Lot-Size-Dependent BOM (STKO-BMEIN); GMP ISO 22716

description: Maximum lot size for which this BOM is valid. Defines the upper bound of the production quantity range for lot-size-dependent BOMs. Null indicates no upper limit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — Lot-Size-Dependent BOM (STKO-BMEIN); GMP ISO 22716

description: Unit of measure for the lot size range (lot_size_from and lot_size_to). Typically matches the base UOM of the finished good (e.g., KG, L, EA).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Lot Size UOM; GS1 Global Standards

description: SAP material number (MATNR) of the finished good or semi-finished product for which this BOM is defined. This is the externally-known product code used across SAP modules (MM, PP, SD, CO) and in EDI transactions with trading partners.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module — Material Master (MARA-MATNR); GS1 GTIN Standards

description: Indicates whether this BOM is used in Material Requirements Planning (MRP) runs for procurement and production scheduling. When true, MRP will explode this BOM to generate dependent requirements for components and raw materials.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/MM Module — MRP (Material Requirements Planning); SAP IBP

description: Free-text notes or comments associated with this BOM header, capturing manufacturing instructions, formulation rationale, regulatory notes, or change justifications that do not fit structured fields. Sourced from SAP BOM header long text.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Header Long Text; ISO 9001 Section 7.5; GMP ISO 22716

description: Four-character SAP plant code identifying the manufacturing facility or production site where this BOM is applicable. Used in MRP, production orders, and supply chain planning (SAP IBP).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/MM Module — Plant (MARC-WERKS); ISO 9001

description: Current lifecycle state of the BOM as managed in the PLM process. 'draft' indicates initial creation, 'in_review' is under engineering/regulatory review, 'approved' is signed off but not yet released to production, 'active' is in use for manufacturing, 'obsolete' is retired, 'superseded' has been replaced by a newer BOM version.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — BOM Status; Veeva Vault PLM; ISO 9001 Section 8.3

description: SAP production version identifier (MKAL-VERID) that links this BOM to a specific routing/recipe and production line. A material may have multiple production versions representing different manufacturing processes or lines at the same plant.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — Production Version (MKAL-VERID); Siemens Opcenter MES

description: Indicates whether all chemical substances in this BOM are compliant with EU REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals) regulation. Mandatory for products sold in the European Union.
reference: EU REACH Regulation (EC No 1907/2006); European Chemicals Agency (ECHA)

description: Status of regulatory approval for this BOM/formulation. Indicates whether the ingredient composition has been reviewed and approved by relevant regulatory bodies (FDA, EU REACH, CPSC). Required before a BOM can be released to active production status.
reference: FDA 21 CFR; EU REACH Regulation; CPSC (Consumer Product Safety Commission); Veeva Vault Regulatory Submissions; ISO 22716

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this BOM record was sourced. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer and enables multi-system reconciliation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/MM Module; Veeva Vault PLM; Siemens Opcenter MES; Oracle Cloud ERP

description: The native primary key or document number of this BOM record in the originating source system (e.g., SAP internal BOM header key combining MATNR+WERKS+STLAL+STLAN). Enables traceability back to the system of record.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — STKO Key Fields (MATNR/WERKS/STLAL/STLAN); Data Lineage

description: Version or revision identifier for the BOM document, enabling traceability of formulation changes over time. Incremented when ingredient quantities, component substitutions, or structural changes are made. Critical for regulatory submissions and GMP compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — Engineering Change Management; ISO 9001 Section 7.5; GMP ISO 22716

description: User ID or name of the person who created this BOM record in SAP S/4HANA or the PLM system. Part of the mandatory audit trail for GMP and SOX compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module — ERNAM; ISO 9001 Section 7.5; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); GMP ISO 22716

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the formulation master record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for all downstream joins and lineage tracking.

Foreign key linking to research.research_formulation. Business justification: Provides audit trail from final product formulation back to its research formulation for change management and compliance reporting.

Reference identifier for the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) document associated with this formulation, stored in Veeva Vault. Required under OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HazCom) and EU REACH for hazardous substances.

description: Name of the primary active ingredient in the formulation (e.g., 'Salicylic Acid', 'Zinc Pyrithione', 'Fluoride'). Required for OTC drug product regulatory filings with FDA and for consumer-facing efficacy claims.

description: Concentration of the primary active ingredient expressed as a weight percentage (w/w%) of the total formulation. Proprietary trade secret data. Governs regulatory classification (OTC drug vs. cosmetic), label claims, and dosage compliance.

description: Free-text or structured declaration of regulated allergens present in the formulation above threshold concentrations (e.g., EU 26 listed fragrance allergens, FDA major food allergens for food-contact products). Required for consumer safety labeling.

description: Calendar date on which the formulation received final commercial approval in the PLM system. Marks the transition from regulatory review to approved lifecycle stage and triggers manufacturing authorization.

description: Reference code linking this formulation to the corresponding Bill of Materials (BOM) in SAP S/4HANA PP/MM. Enables traceability between the approved formulation recipe and the manufacturing BOM used for production planning and Material Requirements Planning (MRP).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/MM; ISO 9001 - Quality Management Systems

description: Standardized color description of the finished formulation as specified in the quality standard (e.g., 'White to off-white', 'Clear colorless', 'Pale yellow'). Used in visual QC inspection and consumer safety documentation.
Timestamp when this formulation record was first created in the source PLM system (Veeva Vault). Provides audit trail for formulation lifecycle tracking and regulatory inspection readiness.

description: Date from which this formulation version is authorized for use in commercial manufacturing. May differ from approval_date when a transition period is required to consume existing raw material stocks.
reference: Veeva Vault PLM; SAP S/4HANA PP; ISO 9001

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the formulation within the Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) system. Sourced from Veeva Vault PLM and used as the cross-system business key across SAP S/4HANA QM and Siemens Opcenter MES.
reference: Veeva Vault PLM; GS1 Global Standards

description: Human-readable descriptive name of the formulation as registered in the PLM system (e.g., 'Moisturizing Body Lotion Base v2 - Fragrance Free'). Used in regulatory submissions, quality documents, and R&D reporting.

description: Indicates whether the formulation contains no animal-derived ingredients or by-products. Supports consumer-facing vegan label claims and retailer listing requirements for vegan-certified product ranges.

description: Reference identifier for the electronic laboratory notebook (ELN) entry or physical lab notebook record documenting the original formulation development experiments. Provides scientific traceability for regulatory submissions and IP protection.
reference: Veeva Vault PLM; FDA 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic Records

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this formulation record in the source PLM system. Used for incremental data loading, change detection, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic Records; ISO 9001; SOX

description: Current stage of the formulation in the Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) workflow, from initial lab development through commercial approval and eventual obsolescence. Governs which business processes may consume this formulation record.
reference: Veeva Vault PLM; ISO 9001 - Quality Management Systems

description: Date on which this formulation version was or is scheduled to be retired and replaced by a newer version. Null for currently active formulations. Used in manufacturing planning to manage version transitions.
reference: Veeva Vault PLM; SAP S/4HANA PP; ISO 9001

description: Maximum acceptable pH value of the formulation as defined in the approved specification. Together with ph_min, defines the pH range tolerance band for quality control (QC) release testing and in-process checks.

description: Minimum acceptable pH value of the formulation as defined in the approved specification. Used in quality control (QC) testing and stability assessments. pH range is a critical quality attribute (CQA) for consumer safety and product efficacy.

reference: FDA CFR Title 21; EU REACH Regulation; ISO 22716

description: Reference code linking this formulation to the originating Research and Development (R&D) / New Product Development (NPD) project in the PLM system. Enables traceability from commercial formulation back to the innovation pipeline.

Current regulatory approval status of the formulation as assessed against applicable jurisdictional requirements (FDA, EU REACH, CPSC). Determines whether the formulation may be used in commercial manufacturing. Distinct from internal PLM lifecycle stage.

description: Regulatory product classification determining the applicable compliance framework and submission pathway. Drives FDA, EPA, or CPSC filing requirements and labeling obligations.

description: Native record identifier of this formulation in the originating source system (Veeva Vault PLM). Enables bidirectional traceability between the Databricks Silver Layer and the system of record for reconciliation and audit purposes.

description: Approved shelf-life stability period of the formulation expressed in months, as determined by accelerated and real-time stability studies. Drives product expiry date calculation, FEFO inventory management, and label 'best before' declarations.

description: Specified storage conditions required to maintain formulation integrity and stability (e.g., 'Store below 25°C, away from direct sunlight', 'Refrigerate at 2-8°C'). Used in warehouse management (WMS), logistics planning, and label compliance.

description: Minimum acceptable viscosity of the formulation measured in centipoise (cPs) at the specified test temperature. Critical quality attribute (CQA) governing product texture, pourability, and consumer experience. Used in QC release testing.

description: Name or employee identifier of the regulatory affairs or R&D professional who approved this ingredient for use in the formulation. Supports GMP audit trail and electronic signature requirements.

description: Date and time when this ingredient line was formally approved for use in the formulation. Provides GMP-compliant audit trail for regulatory inspections and quality management system records.
reference: ISO 22716; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault PLM

description: Directions for use as printed on the label (e.g., application method, dosage, frequency, preparation instructions). Required for regulated product categories and consumer safety.

description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault for the controlled label specification document. Provides direct traceability to the system of record for regulatory submissions and quality documents.
reference: Veeva Vault Quality Documents; ISO 9001 Document Control

description: All warning and precautionary statements required on the label (e.g., 'Keep out of reach of children', 'Flammable', allergen warnings, GHS hazard statements). Mandatory for consumer safety compliance.

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each PLM stage transition event record. Primary key of the plm_transition table.

description: Reference to the brand under which the SKU or formulation is being developed or managed. Supports brand-level NPD pipeline reporting and portfolio analytics.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Consumer Goods Brand Management

description: Reference to the internal user (employee or system account) who initiated or triggered this lifecycle stage transition. Supports audit trail and accountability requirements.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; SOX Audit Trail

description: Reference to the specific formulation version associated with this lifecycle transition, applicable when the transition is driven by a formulation change rather than a product-level event.
reference: Veeva Vault PLM; ISO 22716 Good Manufacturing Practices for Cosmetics

description: Reference to the NPD project or innovation initiative under which this lifecycle transition is occurring. Links the transition to the broader NPD pipeline for portfolio reporting and resource tracking.
Reference to the SKU or product item undergoing the lifecycle stage transition. Links to the product master record.
reference: GS1 Global Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: The date on which the gate review approval was formally granted for this lifecycle stage transition. Distinct from transition_date which records when the transition was executed.
reference: ISO 9001; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; SAP PLM

description: The formal approval document number, change control reference, or gate review authorization code associated with this transition. Used for cross-referencing with quality management and regulatory submission records in Veeva Vault.
reference: Veeva Vault Quality Documents; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 9001

description: Additional free-text commentary entered by the triggering user or approver at the time of the transition, capturing context not covered by structured fields. Supplements gate_review_notes with informal observations.
The timestamp at which this PLM transition record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.

The PLM lifecycle stage from which the SKU or formulation is transitioning. Standard stage codes: Ideation, Concept, Feasibility, Development, Pilot, Scale-Up, Launch, Active, Renovation, Discontinuation, Archived. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Ideation|Concept|Feasibility|Development|Pilot|Scale-Up|Launch|Active|Renovation|Discontinuation|Archived — promote to reference product]

Detailed breakdown of individual gate criteria evaluation results, capturing which specific criteria passed, failed, or were waived during the stage-gate review. Supports granular NPD governance reporting.

Overall outcome of the gate criteria checklist validation performed at the stage-gate review. Pass: all mandatory criteria met; Conditional Pass: approved with conditions or waivers; Fail: one or more mandatory criteria not met; Not Evaluated: gate review not yet conducted.

Structured or free-text notes recorded during the stage-gate review meeting, capturing key decisions, conditions of approval, open action items, and reviewer commentary. Provides the qualitative audit trail for NPD governance.
reference: ISO 9001 Stage-Gate Governance; SAP PLM; Veeva Vault

description: Indicates whether this lifecycle transition was processed under an expedited or fast-track NPD process, bypassing standard gate review timelines. Common for regulatory-driven reformulations or urgent market responses.
Classification code identifying the product category (e.g., personal care, household cleaning, health) to which the SKU belongs. Enables category-level NPD pipeline analysis and regulatory routing.
reference: GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC); SAP S/4HANA MM

description: The reference number or docket identifier for the regulatory submission associated with this lifecycle transition (e.g., FDA 510(k) number, EU REACH dossier ID). Populated when regulatory_submission_required is True.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU REACH Regulation; Veeva Vault Regulatory Submissions

description: Indicates whether this lifecycle stage transition triggers a mandatory regulatory submission or notification (e.g., FDA pre-market notification, EU REACH registration update, CPSC safety report). Drives regulatory workflow routing.
